column5: source
column6: target

column5: I can't believe I'd say something like that.\nAll my life, I've been raised to believe in the spirits.\nBut now, the best thing to do, is throw that belief away?
column6: 真不敢相信我会说出这种话。\n我这一生，都被教导要信仰灵。\n可如今，最好的做法，竟是抛弃这份信仰？

column5: It's been over twenty years since the idol went dark...\nI can't say that I've seen Valinorth get any colder.\nThere's more to this — there has to be.
column6: 灵像熄灭已经二十多年了……\n我却没觉得瓦利诺斯变冷了多少。\n这背后另有隐情——一定有的。

column5: If they don't protect the land, then what does an idol do?\nThey need to have {i}some{/i} sort of purpose, right?\nAll of that energy, packed in one small thing.
column6: 如果它们不守护这片土地，那灵像到底是做什么的？\n它们总得有{i}某种{/i}用途吧？\n那么多能量，全都塞在一个小小的东西里。

column5: Anyway, I need to study more.\nI'll get back to you on that in the future.
column6: 总之，我得再多研究研究。\n以后我会再跟你谈这件事。

column5: Remember what we talked about last time?\nWhether or not we should be open with the people?\nI was worried that they'd use us to their own ends.
column6: 还记得我们上次聊的吗？\n我们该不该对民众坦诚？\n我当时担心他们会利用我们达成自己的目的。

column5: The ability to foresee the future, and change it?\nThat's too powerful. People would pay almost any price.\nAt least, that's what I thought — before you changed my mind.
column6: 预见未来、并改变未来的能力？\n那太强大了。人们几乎愿意付出任何代价。\n至少，在你改变我的想法之前，我是这么想的。

column5: Hiding it from the people? That's just as bad as lying.\nWhen we take down The Triumvirate, we need them to trust us.\nThey'll be placing the world in the hands of entirely new rulers.
column6: 对民众隐瞒？那和撒谎一样恶劣。\n等我们推翻三人执政团时，需要他们信任我们。\n他们正要把这个世界交到一群全新的统治者手中。

column5: Being open is the best course of action.\nI'm glad you changed my mind, to be honest.\nI have a feeling that hiding it would be {i}way{/i} too hard.
column6: 坦诚才是最好的选择。\n说实话，我很高兴你说服了我。\n我总觉得，隐瞒这件事会{i}太{/i}难了。

column5: The ability to forsee the future, and change it?\nThat's too powerful. People would pay almost any price.\nI'm glad you shared the same opinion. We can't tell the people.
column6: 预见未来、并改变未来的能力？\n那太强大了。人们几乎愿意付出任何代价。\n很高兴你也是这么想的。我们不能告诉民众。

column5: You're {i}so{/i} important to this mission, [firstname].\nWe can't have people vying for your skill and attention.\nEspecially if they resort to stuff like kidnapping, or bribing.
column6: 你在这场任务中{i}太{/i}重要了，[firstname]。\n我们不能让人来争夺你的能力和关注。\n尤其是当他们不惜用绑架或贿赂这种手段的时候。

column5: You're {i}so{/i} important to this mission, [firstname].\nWe can't have people vying for your skill and attention.\nEspecially if they resort to stuff like kidnapping, or bribing.
column6: 你在这场任务中{i}太{/i}重要了，[firstname]。\n我们不能让人来争夺你的能力和关注。\n尤其是当他们不惜用绑架或贿赂这种手段的时候。

column5: Sorry to sound so scary, but it's a {i}real{/i} possibility.\nThat's why it's probably best for us to remain anonymous.\nHowever, I have a feeling we can't stay that way forever.
column6: 抱歉说得这么吓人，但这是{i}真实{/i}存在的可能。\n所以我们最好还是保持匿名。\n不过，我总觉得我们不可能永远这样下去。

column5: Damek is wasting no time telling everybody who we are.\nIt's only a matter of time until word spreads to the rest of Mazeo.\nWe'll need to come up with some kind of system, or something.
column6: 达梅克一刻不停地到处宣扬我们是谁。\n消息传遍马泽奥其余地方只是时间问题。\n我们得想出某种制度，或者别的什么办法。

column5: Our main cause is helping Damek and The Rebellion.\nBut when people hear who you are, and come for help?\nWhat should we do then? Honestly, I'm at a loss.
column6: 我们的主要目标是帮助达梅克和反抗军。\n可要是人们听说了你的身份，跑来求助呢？\n那时我们该怎么办？老实说，我一筹莫展。

column5: Maybe I'll talk to him and see what he says.\nIt's possible that I'm just being paranoid, right?\nBut everyone says that Mazeans can be ruthless.
column6: 也许我该找他谈谈，看看他怎么说。\n也许只是我多虑了，对吧？\n可大家都说，马泽奥人可能会很无情。

column5: I just want to help people, {i}and{/i} ensure your safety.\nThere must be a way to do both, and I know I'll find it.\nLet's change the subject, this is really stressing me out.
column6: 我只想帮助别人，{i}同时{/i}保证你的安全。\n一定有办法两全其美，我知道我会找到的。\n我们换个话题吧，这真让我压力很大。

column5: She smiles, yet gives off concern at the same time.{w}\nIt's good that she was thinking about this kind of stuff.{w}\nRemaining resolute in these circumstances was admirable.
column6: 她微笑着，却又透着担忧。{w}\n她能在想这些事，是件好事。{w}\n在这样的处境下还能如此坚定，令人钦佩。

column5: This HQ is a pretty nice place, huh?\nI'm surprised that those suits of armor built this.\nLook — there's a bed here. Why would they need that?
column6: 这总部真是个好地方，对吧？\n没想到那些盔甲竟然建了这里。\n你看——这里还有张床。他们要床做什么？

column5: Damek said they want to live again.\nBut there must be more to it than that.\nIt's so intricate, and clearly built for an army.
column6: 达梅克说他们想再度活过来。\n但事情肯定不止如此。\n这里如此精巧，显然是为一支军队建造的。

column5: I really think they wanted to help us out.\nThat's why they built this place the way it is.\nThey must've {i}known{/i} what was going to happen.
column6: 我真的觉得他们是想帮我们。\n所以他们才把这里建成这样。\n他们一定{i}早就知道{/i}会发生什么。

column5: But that also means they're defying The Triumvirate. \nWhat if we could use their own honor guard against them?\nThough, to be honest, I still feel a bit hesitant using that term.
column6: 但这也意味着他们在违抗三人执政团。\n要是我们能利用他们自己的荣誉卫队来对付他们呢？\n不过说实话，用这个词我还是有点犹豫。

column5: After what they've done to us? There's no honor {i}left{/i} to protect.\nThey've condemned the souls of so many victims to servitude.\nI guess it was only a matter of time before they rebelled, too.
column6: 看看他们对我们做了什么？早就没什么荣誉{i}可{/i}守护了。\n他们把那么多受害者的灵魂判为奴役。\n我想他们迟早也会反抗的。

column5: She sighs and sits down on the bed.{w}\nI slowly walk over and sit down beside her.
column6: 她叹了口气，在床上坐下。{w}\n我慢慢走过去，在她身旁坐下。

column5: Look at me, all business as usual.\nMaybe people are right — maybe I need to unwind.\nLife can't be any fun if you never take a break, right?
column6: 看看我，还是照常忙个不停。\n也许大家说得对——也许我该放松一下。\n要是从不停下来歇歇，生活哪还有乐趣，对吧？

column5: I know, I know...\nBut I wouldn't know where to start.\nThere's so much on my \"to-do\" list.
column6: 我知道，我知道……\n可我不知道该从哪儿开始。\n我的“待办清单”上事情太多了。

column5: Together...? Yeah, I can do that.\nI just wouldn't know where to start.\nThere's so much on my \"to-do\" list.
column6: 一起……？好啊，我可以。\n只是我不知道该从哪儿开始。\n我的“待办清单”上事情太多了。

column5: You're not the first person to tell me that...\nBut unwinding...? I wouldn't know where to start.\nThere's just so much on my \"to-do\" list.
column6: 你不是第一个这么跟我说的人……\n可放松……？我不知道该从哪儿开始。\n我的“待办清单”上事情实在太多了。

column5: Trust me, I'd rather not wait that long.\nIt's just — I wouldn't really know where to start.\nThere's so much on my \"to-do\" list.
column6: 相信我，我也不想等那么久。\n只是——我真的不知道该从哪儿开始。\n我的“待办清单”上事情太多了。

column5: Then what should I do...?\nHonestly, I wouldn't know where to start.\nThere's so much on my \"to-do\" list.
column6: 那我该怎么办……？\n老实说，我不知道该从哪儿开始。\n我的“待办清单”上事情太多了。

column5: I guess I should start from the top, huh?
column6: 我想我该从头开始，对吧？

column5: She motions to the table. There's a bottle of wine on it.
column6: 她朝桌子示意。桌上放着一瓶葡萄酒。

column5: Fortaime has been bugging me about this for a while.\nI guess a drink or two will do plenty to help me unwind.\nWant to keep me company? It's better than staying alone.
column6: 福泰姆为这事念叨我好一阵子了。\n我想喝上一两杯，应该足够让我放松。\n愿意陪陪我吗？总比一个人待着好。

column5: I nod, and we move from the bed to the table.{w}\nShe pops open the bottle, and pours each of us a glass.{w}\nHowever, she doesn't sip. She seems hesitant.
column6: 我点点头，我们从床边移到桌旁。{w}\n她啪地打开瓶塞，给我们各倒了一杯。{w}\n可她没喝。她似乎有些犹豫。

column5: Shouldn't we have a toast or something?\nI mean — we're supposed to drink for a cause, right?\nI'm new to this, so I'll let you do the honors, [firstname].
column6: 我们是不是该敬个酒什么的？\n我是说——喝酒总该有个由头，对吧？\n我是新手，所以这份荣幸就交给你了，[firstname]。

column5: Shouldn't we have a toast or something?\nI mean — we're supposed to drink for a cause, right?\nI'm new to this, so I'll let you do the honors, [firstname].
column6: 我们是不是该敬个酒什么的？\n我是说——喝酒总该有个由头，对吧？\n我是新手，所以这份荣幸就交给你了，[firstname]。

column5: I couldn't have said it better myself...
column6: 我再怎么想，也说不出比这更好的了……

column5: We each take a sip, and begin to wile away the hours.{w}\nI help get her mind off of work, and we talk for a long time.{w}\nAfter that, I see myself back to the crew quarters — happy.
column6: 我们各自啜了一口，开始消磨时光。{w}\n我帮她暂时放下工作，我们聊了很久。{w}\n之后，我满心欢喜地回到船员舱。

column5: I enter Ulric's room, and he's laying on his bed, relaxed.{w}\nBottles of alcohol line the table nearby, some empty, some full.{w}\nHe hears me enter, and immediately rises up, grabbing his sword.
column6: 我走进乌尔里克的房间，他正放松地躺在床上。{w}\n旁边的桌上摆满酒瓶，有的空了，有的还是满的。{w}\n他听见我进来，立刻起身，抓起自己的剑。

column5: Who's there!?
column6: 谁在那儿！？

column5: But as soon as he notices it's me, he relaxes with a sigh.{w}\nLoosening his grip on his sword, he puts it aside.{w}\nHe was a bit paranoid, but with reason.
column6: 但一发现是我，他就松了口气，放松下来。{w}\n他松开握剑的手，把剑放到一边。{w}\n他有点疑神疑鬼，但情有可原。

column5: Sorry, you never know when someone might attack.\nI don't normally doze off too much — for that reason alone.\nIt's nice to see you, though. I had a good time at the tavern.
column6: 抱歉，谁也不知道什么时候会有人来袭。\n正因如此，我平常不会睡得太沉。\n不过见到你真好。那天在酒馆我玩得很开心。

column5: He stands up, and walks over to the table.{w}\nWith a large swig from another bottle, he lets out a refreshing sigh.{w}\nHe must not have much downtime, but today was an \"off\" day.
column6: 他站起身，走到桌边。{w}\n他从另一只瓶子里灌了一大口，舒畅地叹了口气。{w}\n他平时一定没什么空闲，不过今天算是“休息日”。

column5: Damek said to relax, so that's what I'm doing.\nI've known him for years, and he's never said that.\nI'm surprised he's not celebrating his new pirate treaty.
column6: 达梅克让我放松，我就照做了。\n我认识他这么多年，他从没说过这种话。\n我倒是奇怪他没在庆祝新签的海盗条约。

column5: Even if he tells us to relax, I doubt that he's doing it.\nHe's probably already waiting for you in the war room.\nDon't worry, I'll try not to keep you here for too long.
column6: 就算他叫我们放松，我猜他自己也没放松。\n他八成已经在作战室等你了。\n别担心，我尽量不把你留太久。

column5: He shuffles bottles aside, looking for something specific.{w}\nIt isn't much longer until he finds a much larger bottle, still full.{w}\nThere's a crimson liquid inside. It seems to be a special wine.
column6: 他把酒瓶拨到一边，在找某样特定的东西。{w}\n没一会儿，他找出一只大得多的瓶子，还是满的。{w}\n里面装着深红色的液体。似乎是种特别的酒。

column5: I've been saving this for a special occasion.\nAnd trust me, Damek giving me the night off is {i}really{/i} special.\nI don't remember the last time I could just sit back and relax.
column6: 这瓶我一直留到特别的日子才喝。\n相信我，达梅克给我放一晚假可是{i}相当{/i}特别的事。\n我都不记得上次能这样闲坐下来放松是什么时候了。

column5: He pops the cork out of the bottle and takes a large swig.{w}\nWeren't you supposed to savor wine, rather than chug it...?
column6: 他拔开瓶塞，痛饮了一大口。{w}\n葡萄酒不是该细细品味，而不是这么灌的吗……？

column5: Alarinthian wine... It's quite delicious.\nI'd say it's the best thing to come from that horrible place.\nIt tastes like juice, but trust me, it sneaks up on you later.
column6: 阿拉林西亚的葡萄酒……相当美味。\n要说那个糟糕地方出过什么好东西，就数它了。\n喝起来像果汁，但相信我，它的后劲会悄悄找上你。

column5: Shall we...?
column6: 来吧……？

column5: He holds out the bottle, offering it to me.{w}\nI accept it, and we both sit down on the edge of the bed.{w}\nTaking turns, we pass the bottle back and forth until its gone.
column6: 他把瓶子递过来，要给我。{w}\n我接过来，我们都在床沿坐下。{w}\n我们轮流着把瓶子来回传，直到喝光。

column5: Wow, that certainly took me back.\nI haven't had a drinking buddy like you in a {i}long{/i} time.\nPeople these days seem to forget about the finer things in life.
column6: 哇，这真让我想起从前。\n我{i}很久{/i}没有像你这样的酒友了。\n如今的人似乎都忘了生活中更美好的东西。

column5: Damek is always saying \"train, train, train\".\nI don't even know if he's capable of taking it easy.\nAt least Salus knew how to balance work and fun.
column6: 达梅克总是说“训练、训练、训练”。\n我都不知道他到底懂不懂什么叫放松。\n至少萨卢斯懂得平衡工作和玩乐。

column5: He goes to take another sip of the wine, trying to get the last drops.{w}\nI wonder how much that cost him — it's probably the best I've ever tasted.
column6: 他又去抿了一口酒，想喝到最后一滴。{w}\n我好奇这瓶花了他多少钱——这大概是我尝过最好的酒了。

column5: I guess I shouldn't bore you with that kind of talk.\nYour time is valuable, and you're choosing to spend it with me.\nSome host I'd be if I sat here and wasted that time of yours.
column6: 我想我不该用这种话让你无聊。\n你的时间很宝贵，而你还选择陪我。\n要是我坐在这儿白白浪费你的时间，那算什么待客之道。

column5: He stands up and places the bottle on the table before sitting down again.{w}\nThe bed is more than big enough to fit the both of us comfortably.{w}\nHe lets out a loud sigh, before crossing his arms.
column6: 他站起来，把瓶子放到桌上，又坐了下来。{w}\n这张床足够大，我们俩躺着都绰绰有余。{w}\n他长叹一声，然后抱起双臂。

column5: I guess that's all I had.\nToo bad — the night is still young.
column6: 我想我的存货就这些了。\n可惜——夜还长着呢。

column5: He laughs softly, looking over in my direction.
column6: 他轻声笑了笑，朝我这边看过来。

column5: Drinking buddies with no drinks? \nThis is a first. What now...?
column6: 酒友没酒了？\n这还是头一遭。接下来干嘛……？

column5: Has it really been this long since Ulric had a friend?{w}\nHe doesn't know what to do, so I give him some direction.{w}\nIt's crazy how much he knows about me, yet I know nothing about him.
column6: 乌尔里克真的已经这么久没有朋友了吗？{w}\n他不知所措，于是我给他指了个方向。{w}\n他对我知道得那么多，我却对他一无所知，真不可思议。

column5: More about me...?\nSo you want me to bore you, huh?
column6: 更多关于我的事……？\n这么说，你想让我烦你，是吧？

column5: He smiles and lays back in the bed, looking up at the ceiling.{w}\nIt's almost like he didn't want to look at me while he spoke.{w}\nAs a courtesy, I lay back as well, and we look up together.
column6: 他笑了笑，向后躺在床上，望着天花板。{w}\n他好像不太想说话时看着我。{w}\n出于礼貌，我也躺了下来，我们一起望向天花板。

column5: Well, I'm probably older than you think.\nBut I prefer to use the term \"experienced\".\nI've seen a lot of combat in my numerous years.
column6: 嗯，我大概比你想象的年纪大。\n不过我更喜欢用“阅历丰富”这个说法。\n这些年我经历过不少战斗。

column5: You kind of grow up alongside battle in Alarinthia.\nThe culture there is so steeped in war, it's impossible to avoid.\nWhen you come of age, you should already be an expert in combat.
column6: 在阿拉林西亚，你几乎是伴着战斗长大的。\n那里的文化浸透了战争，避无可避。\n等你成年时，本该已经是格斗的行家了。

column5: I was — but I chose to leave Alarinthia behind as soon as I could.\nMy parents wanted me to stay; but I think they wanted it for {i}them{/i}.\nI came to the mainland because I knew it would be the best for {i}me{/i}.
column6: 我是——但我一有机会就选择离开阿拉林西亚。\n我父母想让我留下；但我觉得他们是为{i}自己{/i}着想。\n我来到大陆，因为我知道这对我{i}自己{/i}最好。

column5: You need to look out for {i}yourself{/i}. Don't let others sway your opinion.\nAt least that's what I told myself. I justified breaking my parents' hearts.\nI can't make it up to them, either. They've been gone for ages.
column6: 你得为{i}自己{/i}打算。别让别人左右你的想法。\n至少我是这么告诉自己的。我用这套说辞为自己伤透父母的心开脱。\n我也没法弥补他们了。他们已经走了很多年。

column5: They were part of a movement that wanted to \"change\" Alarinthia.\n\"Things would be better in the hands of the wise, not the strong.\"\nAn admirable view — unless you're surrounded by the strong.
column6: 他们属于一个想要“改变”阿拉林西亚的运动。\n“让智者掌权，而非强者，世道会更好。”\n这观点令人钦佩——除非你四周都是强者。

column5: And surrounded they were. They were killed for their beliefs.\nThat's why I hate Alarinthia more than anything; and the way it's run.\nI told myself I'd come to the mainland and practice my swordplay.
column6: 而他们确实被强者包围。他们因自己的信念被杀。\n所以我才最恨阿拉林西亚，恨它的统治方式。\n我告诉自己，我要来大陆磨练剑术。

column5: I'd only ever return when I was strong enough to win.\nIf I could become the ruler of Alarinthia, I would change their laws.\nEvery leader has that ability, but they only care about their own power.
column6: 我只会在强大到足以取胜时才回去。\n如果我能成为阿拉林西亚的统治者，我就要改变他们的法律。\n每个领袖都有这个能力，可他们只在乎自己的权力。

column5: It's always a battle of the strong against the wise.\nI wanted to go back to that land, both strong {i}and{/i} wise.\nA ruler with a different outlook? He could change {i}everything{/i}.
column6: 这始终是强者与智者之争。\n我想回到那片土地，既强大{i}又{/i}睿智。\n一个想法不同的统治者？他能改变{i}一切{/i}。

column5: It's just the alcohol talking right now, by the way.\nThe childish dream of a young man — that's all it was.\nThis world offers no quarter to men blind on ambition.
column6: 顺便说一句，现在不过是酒话罢了。\n一个年轻人的幼稚梦想——仅此而已。\n这世界不会对野心蒙蔽双眼的人手下留情。

column5: He tilts his head to look at me.
column6: 他歪过头看我。

column5: And so, we offer no quarter in return.\nThis war — it's already taken so much from us.\nI find myself asking, how much more will it take...?
column6: 所以，我们也绝不手下留情。\n这场战争——已经从我们身上夺走太多了。\n我不禁自问，它还要夺走多少……？

column5: He leans in closer, and his words become softer.
column6: 他靠得更近，话音也变得更轻柔。

column5: If anything, at least it's taught me something important.\nWe can only truly enjoy what we have right in front of us.\nOnce it leaves our sight, we may never see it again.
column6: 至少它教给了我一件重要的事。\n我们只能真正珍惜眼前拥有的一切。\n一旦它离开视线，也许就再也见不到了。

column5: He raises a hand and runs it along the side of my face, smiling at me.{w}\nI can tell he's nervous, but so am I. I know exactly what's coming.
column6: 他抬起手，沿着我的脸颊轻轻抚过，对我微笑。{w}\n我看得出他紧张，我也一样。我清楚地知道接下来会发生什么。

column5: We just need to live in the moment, right?\nAt the end of the day, that's all we really have.\nSomething special we can share, and never forget.
column6: 我们只需要活在当下，对吧？\n说到底，我们真正拥有的也就只有此刻。\n一份能彼此分享、永不遗忘的特别之物。

column5: He leans in closer, and I smell the sweet of the wine on his breath.{w}\nI lean in too, signaling my consent; and we quickly surrender to passion.{w}\nOur lips press together. Once, twice, and then I'm unable to keep count.
column6: 他靠得更近，我闻到他呼吸里甜美的酒香。{w}\n我也靠过去，以示默许；我们很快便沉溺于激情。{w}\n我们的唇贴在一起。一次，两次，然后我就数不清了。

column5: The warmth of our bodies intertwined is all I'm capable of focusing on.{w}\nHe was right. No matter what happened, we'd always have this memory.{w}\nI wanted to get to know him better, and that's what I did — without words.
column6: 我唯一能专注感受的，是彼此交缠的身体的温暖。{w}\n他说得对。无论发生什么，我们都将永远拥有这段记忆。{w}\n我想更了解他，而我也做到了——无需言语。

column5: Hopefully not too much...
column6: 但愿别太过头……

column5: I turn to respond, but I notice his eyes are closed.{w}\nWas he so tired that he could fall asleep almost instantly?{w}\nI wonder if I should wake him up, but decide to let him rest.
column6: 我转头想回应，却发现他闭着眼。{w}\n他是不是累到几乎瞬间就能睡着？{w}\n我犹豫要不要叫醒他，最后还是决定让他休息。

column5: Slowly getting out of the bed, I tiptoe my way to the door.{w}\nIt's been a long journey for him, too. He deserves this.{w}\nI exit as silently as I can, ready to continue on my way.
column6: 我慢慢下床，踮着脚走向门口。{w}\n于他而言这一路也很漫长。这是他应得的。{w}\n我尽可能悄无声息地离开，准备继续赶路。

column5: But I learned more about him, so I'm happy.{w}\nMaybe he'd get to change Alarinthia in the end.{w}\nAfter we defeat The Triumvirate, {i}anything{/i} is possible.
column6: 但我对他有了更多了解，所以我很开心。{w}\n也许他最终真能改变阿拉林西亚。{w}\n等我们击败三人执政团后，{i}一切{/i}皆有可能。

column5: I enter Pro's room, and see him sitting down.{w}\nHe's hunched over a piece of paper, scribbling notes down on it.{w}\nIt appears to be some sort of legal looking document.
column6: 我走进普洛的房间，看见他正坐着。{w}\n他伏在一张纸上，匆匆写着笔记。{w}\n那似乎是某种看起来像法律文件的文书。

column5: An opened bottle of wine sits next to him, and it's still full.{w}\nTwo wine glasses sit on the table, on opposite sides of each other.{w}\nUpon hearing my entrance, he looks up at me and smirks.
column6: 他身旁放着一瓶开了封的酒，还是满的。{w}\n桌上摆着两只酒杯，分放在两侧。{w}\n听到我进来，他抬起头，冲我一笑。

column5: I knew you'd come sooner or later.\nGood thing the wine didn't get too warm.\nHave a seat — this is some good vintage stuff.
column6: 我就知道你会来。\n还好酒没被焐得太热。\n坐吧——这可是上好的陈酿。

column5: I pull out the chair and sit across from Pro.{w}\nAs soon as I sit down, he starts pouring us some wine.{w}\nIt's a dark crimson red, and appears to be quite thick.
column6: 我拉开椅子，在普洛对面坐下。{w}\n我刚坐定，他就开始给我们倒酒。{w}\n酒色深红，显得颇为浓稠。

column5: At least, that's what the guy told me.\nI just asked for their most expensive wine.\nThat job from before? I made more than I thought.
column6: 至少，那家伙是这么跟我说的。\n我直接点了他们最贵的酒。\n之前那活儿？我赚的比预想的多。

column5: I asked myself what I should do with all of it.\nI mean, there was a ton to spare even after buying food.\nAll I could think of, was \"share a drink with my new friend\".
column6: 我问自己这么多钱该怎么花。\n我是说，买完吃的还剩下大把。\n我唯一想到的，就是“跟我新交的朋友喝一杯”。

column5: So, here we are.\nHopefully it's something you enjoy.\nI'd hate to buy you a treat you didn't like.
column6: 所以，就有了现在。\n但愿这酒合你口味。\n我可不想买了你不喜欢的东西来招待你。

column5: Of course I didn't — it's a gift!\nKinda loses its meaning if I have to do it.\nI wanted to get things off to a better start, you know?
column6: 我当然没有——这是礼物！\n要是还得我开口要，那就没意义了。\n我想给我们开个更好的头，懂吗？

column5: Wait — I didn't do that already...?\nI already have this whole \"lovable rogue\" thing mastered.\nIt was just a matter of sealing the deal with some wine.
column6: 等等——我不是已经这么做过了吗……？\n我这套“讨喜的浪荡子”人设早就炉火纯青了。\n就差用点酒来把事敲定。

column5: Yeah, especially under Damek's wing.\nHe'll have you training like its going out of style.\nI just wanted to show you a good time before all that.
column6: 是啊，尤其是落在达梅克手下。\n他会让你练到练不动为止。\n我就想在那一堆苦差事之前让你开心一下。

column5: No problem! It's the least I could do.\nYou'll have a lot on your plate in the coming days.\nI thought I'd be a good guy and help you unwind beforehand.
column6: 没问题！这是我起码该做的。\n接下来几天你会有很多事要忙。\n我想当个好人，先帮你放松放松。

column5: Last time we hung out, I didn't really get the chance.\nI was worried I'd scare you away when you found out what I do.\nIt's dirty work, but it helps us survive. {i}Somebody{/i} has to do it, right?
column6: 上次我们聚的时候，我其实没找到机会。\n我担心你一旦知道我是干什么的，就会被吓跑。\n这是脏活，可它能帮我们活下去。总得{i}有人{/i}来做，对吧？

column5: There's a {i}big{/i} difference between me and a regular swindler, though.\nI do it because we need to survive. They do it for fun, and riches.\nAfter the war is over, I won't need to do this stuff anymore.
column6: 不过，我和普通骗子有{i}很大{/i}的区别。\n我干这个是因为我们需要活下去。他们干这个是为了玩乐和钱财。\n战争结束后，我就不用再干这些了。

column5: Trust me, I {i}long{/i} for that day to come.\nI want to just kick back, and work on my writing.\nRight now, I only have time for {i}this{/i} kind of stuff.
column6: 相信我，我{i}盼{/i}着那天到来。\n我想悠闲地坐下来，专心搞我的写作。\n而现在，我只有时间忙{i}这些{/i}事。

column5: He motions to the paper he was writing on, and sighs.
column6: 他朝自己刚写的那张纸示意，叹了口气。

column5: Organized blackmail, pretty much.\nThat guy I mentioned last time? I was able to bribe him.\nHe gave us tons of money to hide his growing misconduct.
column6: 说白了，就是有组织的敲诈。\n我上次提到的那个人？我成功贿赂了他。\n他给了我们一大笔钱，用来掩盖他越来越多的劣迹。

column5: Of course, that makes it sound so... \"bad.\"\nBut you always need to get everything in writing.\nSo we found a better way to word it. Listen to this.
column6: 当然，这么说听起来太……“难听”了。\n但凡事总得白纸黑字写下来。\n所以我们换了个更好的说法。你听听。

column5: \"I offer Pro this sum of money in exchange for discretion.\"\nSee? Doesn't sound too much like shady business, does it?\nInformation is a {i}huge{/i} market, and so is stopping the flow of it.
column6: “我向普洛支付此款，以换取其守口如瓶。”\n看吧？听起来不太像见不得人的勾当，对吧？\n情报是{i}巨大{/i}的市场，阻断情报流通也是。

column5: Everyone is so caught up on {i}doing{/i} stuff to make money.\nAnd here I am, able to make it all by {i}staying{/i} my hand.\nYou just need to think outside the box a bit, [firstname].
column6: 人人都忙着{i}动手做事{/i}来赚钱。\n而我呢，只要{i}按兵不动{/i}就能赚到。\n你只需要稍微跳出框框想一想，[firstname]。

column5: Everyone is so caught up on {i}doing{/i} stuff to make money.\nAnd here I am, able to make it all by {i}staying{/i} my hand.\nYou just need to think outside the box a bit, [firstname].
column6: 人人都忙着{i}动手做事{/i}来赚钱。\n而我呢，只要{i}按兵不动{/i}就能赚到。\n你只需要稍微跳出框框想一想，[firstname]。

column5: Anyway, enough about that.\nWe should talk about the {i}important{/i} stuff.\nHow are you enjoying the new HQ so far?
column6: 总之，这些就说到这儿。\n我们该聊点{i}重要的{/i}事。\n到目前为止，你觉得新总部怎么样？

column5: Yeah, I thought the same thing.\nAlthough, I really hesitate to call it \"new\".\nWe basically lived here before getting the deed.
column6: 是啊，我也这么想。\n不过，我实在不太想管它叫“新”。\n拿到地契之前，我们基本就住在这儿了。

column5: It was more of a formality than anything.\nAnyway, that's not really important.\nI'm glad you like it. We're stuck here.
column6: 那更多只是走个形式。\n总之，那并不重要。\n你喜欢就好。我们可被困在这儿了。

column5: Oh, is that so...?\nI guess the drink really won you over, then.\nThat's what the guy told me — it was a \"romantic\" wine.
column6: 哦，是吗……？\n看来这酒确实把你征服了。\n那家伙就是这么跟我说的——这是款“浪漫”的酒。

column5: I mean, not that I was trying to be romantic.\nAww jeeze, I hope you don't get the wrong idea.\nUnless it's the right idea. Then please, by all means.
column6: 我是说，我不是故意要弄得很浪漫。\n哎呀，但愿你别误会。\n除非那误会是对的。那你就尽情误会吧。

column5: Damek, cleaning...?\nPlease! He's way too busy for that.\nIt's the recruits who are slacking off, actually.
column6: 达梅克，打扫……？\n得了吧！他忙得很，哪有空干这个。\n其实偷懒的是那些新兵。

column5: There's a schedule in place for cleaning.\nIt accounts for every room, and every surface.\nOf course, it seems like nobody follows it.
column6: 打扫是有排班表的。\n每个房间、每处表面都算在内。\n当然，似乎没人照着执行。

column5: Yeah, I just miss the sun.\nBut I leave every day for my workout routine.\nI run all the way to the town square and back.
column6: 是啊，我就是想念阳光。\n不过我每天都会出去锻炼。\n我一路跑到镇广场再跑回来。

column5: Most people call me crazy, but they're just not used to it.\nYou can get used to {i}anything{/i} if you do it long enough.\nI remember when I first started. I was a total mess.
column6: 大多数人都说我疯了，可他们只是不习惯而已。\n只要坚持够久，{i}任何事{/i}都能习惯。\n我记得刚开始那会儿，我简直一团糟。

column5: We continue to talk while taking slow sips of wine.{w}\nThe atmosphere in here is a lot better than back at the tavern.{w}\nAnd it feels like we're getting to know each other far more.
column6: 我们一边慢慢啜着酒，一边继续聊。{w}\n这里的气氛比酒馆好多了。{w}\n感觉我们对彼此的了解也深了许多。

column5: Honestly, I'm having a really great time.\nIt's not often I get to put everything on pause.\nBut right now? I don't have a care in the world.
column6: 老实说，我真的很开心。\n我很少有机会把一切都暂停下来。\n但现在？我无忧无虑。

column5: If we have more time, want to do this again?\nI mean — time might be pretty scarce in the future.\nBut what little time I have, I'd totally spend with you.
column6: 要是以后还有时间，想再来一次吗？\n我是说——以后时间可能会很紧。\n但我只要有那么一点时间，也全都会花在你身上。

column5: That settles it, then!\nI'm glad we were able to push past that awkward stage.\nYou know, the whole \"hey, I'm a swindler!\" part of this...?
column6: 那就这么定了！\n很高兴我们能跨过那个尴尬的阶段。\n就是那句“嘿，我是个骗子！”的部分……？

column5: I promise it'll be good times and wine from here on out.\nThough I still think you should be my workout partner...!\nNext time, maybe I'll challenge you to a little race.
column6: 我保证，从现在起就只有好时光和美酒。\n不过我仍然觉得你该当我的锻炼搭档……！\n下次，也许我找你赛跑一小段。

column5: I mean, if you want to put a label on it, sure.\nBut I was just thinking it'd be nice to spend more time together.\nWe're finally past that whole \"awkward\" part of introductions.
column6: 我是说，你要是想给它贴个标签，也行。\n我只是觉得，能多花点时间在一起就好了。\n我们总算度过了自我介绍那段“尴尬”期。

column5: I mean, I had to come clean about being a swindler, right?\nI'd rather do it right out of the gate than surprise you later on.\nWe can get to know each other more, now, and see if we click.
column6: 我是说，我总得坦白自己是骗子，对吧？\n与其日后再让你吃惊，不如一开始就说清楚。\n现在我们可以多了解彼此，看看合不合得来。

column5: Well, not {i}this{/i} particular wine, but sure.\nThis was just a special occasion for me, you know?\nWine with The Seer. Not everybody gets to do that.
column6: 嗯，倒不是说{i}这款{/i}酒，但行吧。\n这对我而言只是个特别的场合，你懂吗？\n和先知共饮。可不是谁都有这机会。

column5: Well, not {i}this{/i} particular wine, but sure.\nThis was just a special occasion for me, you know?\nWine with The Seeress. Not everybody gets to do that.
column6: 嗯，倒不是说{i}这款{/i}酒，但行吧。\n这对我而言只是个特别的场合，你懂吗？\n和先知共饮。可不是谁都有这机会。

column5: But I don't mean to stroke your ego, or anything like that.\nBig heads don't win wars. It's more like... big minds.\nOf course, that sword is sure gonna help out a lot.
column6: 我不是想给你戴高帽，或者别的什么。\n自大赢不了战争，靠的其实是……大智慧。\n当然，那把剑肯定能帮上大忙。

column5: Yikes. Understandable, yet firm.\nI'll let you come see me at {i}your{/i} convenience.\nAs long as we're here, my doors will be open for you.
column6: 哎哟。可以理解，但也很坚决。\n那就随{i}你{/i}方便时来找我吧。\n只要我们还在，我的门随时为你敞开。

column5: I'm glad you're into the idea.\nI didn't want to come on too strong with the wine.\nBut as long as my profession didn't scare you, I'm good.
column6: 很高兴你接受这个主意。\n我不太想用酒表现得太强势。\n不过只要我的职业没吓到你，我就放心了。

column5: I mean, we got past the whole \"me being a swindler\" thing.\nSo I guess no matter what I throw at you, you'll be unfazed.\nI like that. A lot of people are {i}way{/i} more unforgiving.
column6: 我是说，我们连“我是个骗子”这关都过了。\n所以我想，不管我抛出什么，你都不会被吓到。\n我喜欢这点。很多人可是{i}远远{/i}更不宽容的。

column5: We keep drinking, until the wine is all gone.{w}\nIt's just casual conversation, nothing too intense.{w}\nBut once we're done, Pro stands up and yawns.
column6: 我们继续喝，直到酒全喝光。{w}\n只是些轻松的闲聊，没什么深重的。{w}\n可等我们喝完，普洛站起身，打了个哈欠。

column5: I guess this is it, then...?\nFor now, of course. It's getting late.\nYou shouldn't keep Damek waiting too long.
column6: 那这次就到这里了……？\n当然是暂时的。天色不早了。\n你不该让达梅克等太久。

column5: As much as I hate to cut this short, I mean...\nIt's nice to just push aside all responsibilities.\nLet's make a habit of it. It'll be like a ritual of ours.
column6: 虽然我很不愿这么早结束，可我是说……\n把一切责任都抛到一边，感觉真好。\n让我们把这变成习惯吧。就当是我们之间的仪式。

column5: He smiles, and I stand up, ready to leave.{w}\nBut I guess he's not ready to see me off just yet.{w}\nRunning forward, he wraps his arms around me.
column6: 他笑了笑，我站起身准备离开。{w}\n可他似乎还没准备好送我走。{w}\n他跑上前，一把抱住我。

column5: Thank you, [firstname].\nNext time, it's a date — just like you said.\nI'll get more wine, and candles. It'll be great.
column6: 谢谢你，[firstname]。\n下次就是约会了——就像你说的。\n我会多备些酒，还有蜡烛。一定会很棒。

column5: Thank you, [firstname].\nNext time, it's a date — just like you said.\nI'll get more wine, and candles. It'll be great.
column6: 谢谢你，[firstname]。\n下次就是约会了——就像你说的。\n我会多备些酒，还有蜡烛。一定会很棒。

column5: He smiles, and I stand up, ready to leave.{w}\nBut I guess he's not ready to see me off just yet.{w}\nRunning forward, he offers me a firm handshake.
column6: 他笑了笑，我站起身准备离开。{w}\n可他似乎还没准备好送我走。{w}\n他跑上前，向我伸出一只有力的手。

column5: Thank you, [firstname].
column6: 谢谢你，[firstname]。

column5: Thank you, [firstname].
column6: 谢谢你，[firstname]。

column5: And with that, he's back to his own business.{w}\nSitting at the table, he's lost in that letter once more.{w}\nI leave the door with a smile on my face. I'm glad we got along.
column6: 说完，他又忙起自己的事。{w}\n他坐在桌边，再次沉浸在那封信里。{w}\n我面带微笑走出门口。很高兴我们相处得不错。

column5: I enter Damek's personal quarters, and see him sitting on his bed.{w}\nHe's gripping something in his hand. It looks shiny, and metallic.{w}\nI take a few steps forward, making my presence known to him.
column6: 我走进达梅克的私人房间，看见他坐在床上。{w}\n他手里紧攥着什么东西，闪闪发亮，像是金属。{w}\n我向前走了几步，让他知道我在。

column5: He immediately jerks in fright, startled by my entrance.{w}\nLooking away from me, he wipes his eyes with haste.{w}\nHe's wearing a wide smile by the time he looks back.
column6: 他立刻吓得一颤，被我的闯入惊到。{w}\n他把脸转向别处，匆忙擦了擦眼睛。{w}\n等他再转回来时，已挂上一脸大大的笑容。

column5: Oh, hey there.\nJust keeping up my habit of not being receptive, I suppose.\nIf I knew you'd be here so fast, I would've put out some food.
column6: 哦，你好啊。\n我想我只是在保持自己不善待客的老毛病。\n早知道你来得这么快，我就备些吃的了。

column5: He stands up and walks to the nearby table.{w}\nAfter placing the object he was holding on it, he lets out a soft laugh.{w}\nI look at it when I get the chance. It appears to be some kind of brooch.
column6: 他站起身，走到旁边的桌旁。{w}\n把手里握着的东西放上去后，他轻轻笑了一声。{w}\n我趁机会看了一眼。那似乎是某种胸针。

column5: I trust our HQ is to your satisfaction?\nHopefully the rebels have been treating you with respect.\nThat blade strapped to your back pretty much gives you away.
column6: 我相信我们的总部还算让你满意吧？\n希望反抗军们一直对你礼敬有加。\n你背上绑着的那把剑，基本就足以表明你的身份了。

column5: Let me know if anybody acts out of turn.\nI won't hesitate to put them in their place, you know.\nYou're our honored guest, and should be treated as such.
column6: 要是有人越矩，就告诉我。\n你知道，我会毫不犹豫地让他们认清自己的位置。\n你是我们尊贵的客人，就该受到这样的对待。

column5: I appreciate it.\nIt's hard to keep tabs on everything, nowadays.\nI'm trying my best, but so much slips through my grasp.
column6: 谢了。\n如今要事事都盯着，太难了。\n我已经尽力了，可太多事从指缝间溜走。

column5: Hey now, don't get used to it.\nYour guest privileges only extend so far.\nAfter today, you'll be under a strict training regiment.
column6: 哎，别习惯了。\n你的客人特权也就到这儿为止。\n从今天起，你就要接受严格的训练了。

column5: Alright, alright — I'm sorry.\nSometimes I'm too nice for my own good.\nDon't worry, I didn't {i}mean{/i} to offend you, [firstname].
column6: 好啦，好啦——我道歉。\n有时候我就是好心得过了头。\n别担心，我不是{i}有意{/i}冒犯你，[firstname]。

column5: Alright, alright — I'm sorry.\nSometimes I'm too nice for my own good.\nDon't worry, I didn't {i}mean{/i} to offend you, [firstname].
column6: 好啦，好啦——我道歉。\n有时候我就是好心得过了头。\n别担心，我不是{i}有意{/i}冒犯你，[firstname]。

column5: If that's what strikes your fancy — then of course.\nI try not to be too ruthless, but sometimes it's necessary.\nIn my position, you need to maintain a certain level of respect.
column6: 要是你喜欢那样——那当然没问题。\n我尽量不做得太狠，但有时那也必要。\n身处我这个位置，你得维持一定的威信。

column5: Fantastic. I guess it's smooth sailing, now.\nAfter some downtime, we need to meet in the war room.\nIt's not too complicated, but I'll give you your training schedule.
column6: 太好了。我想现在一切顺利了。\n休息一阵后，我们得在作战室碰面。\n事情不复杂，不过我会把训练日程给你。

column5: He pulls out two chairs and proceeds to sit down.{w}\nTaking the side closest to the brooch he laid down, he looks up at me.
column6: 他拉出两把椅子，坐了下来。{w}\n他坐在靠近那枚胸针放下的一侧，抬头看我。

column5: Care to join me?\nI wouldn't mind getting to know you a little better.\nYou're more than just The Seer, after all.
column6: 愿意陪我坐坐吗？\n我倒不介意多了解你一点。\n毕竟，你不只是“先知”而已。

column5: Care to join me?\nI wouldn't mind getting to know you a little better.\nYou're more than just The Seeress, after all.
column6: 愿意陪我坐坐吗？\n我倒不介意多了解你一点。\n毕竟，你不只是“先知”而已。

column5: It's rude of us to treat you like some sort of symbol.\nI know some of my troops do that to me, since I'm the General.\nBut there's more beneath the surface. So much more.
column6: 把你当作某种象征来对待，是我们失礼。\n我知道有些部下也这样对我，因为我是将军。\n可表象之下还有更多。多得多。

column5: I nod and take a seat in the chair opposite Damek.{w}\nHe smiles and leans forward, displaying an attentive pose.{w}\nHis lack of speech makes me realize that it's my turn to speak.
column6: 我点点头，在达梅克对面的椅子上坐下。{w}\n他微笑着前倾身子，摆出一副专注倾听的姿态。{w}\n他不出声，让我意识到该我开口了。

column5: I tell him everything I can, pretty much summing up my life.{w}\nI tell him how I met Fortaime and Valessa, and how we grew up.{w}\nBut most importantly, I tell him about the loss of our parents.
column6: 我把能说的都告诉了他，基本上把自己的人生都讲了一遍。{w}\n我讲了如何遇见福泰姆和瓦莱莎，以及我们一起长大的经历。{w}\n但最重要的是，我告诉了他我们失去双亲的事。

column5: As soon as he hears that story, I can see him tense up.{w}\nHe reaches for the brooch, and clenches it tightly in his hand.{w}\nAfter a few moments of holding onto it, he starts to relax.
column6: 他一听到这话，我就能看出他绷紧了。{w}\n他伸手去够那枚胸针，紧紧攥在手里。{w}\n握了一会儿之后，他才渐渐放松下来。

column5: The Occupation...\nWe all lost something special that day.\nBut some of us lost far more than others.
column6: 占领……\n那一天，我们都失去了某些珍贵的东西。\n但有些人失去的远比其他人多。

column5: What an unlucky day to be in Mazeo, huh?\nYour parents could've easily avoided that mess.\nMine however? Well, not so much. It's complicated.
column6: 那天恰好在马泽奥，可真不走运，是吧？\n你的父母本可以轻易避开那场灾难。\n我的父母呢？唉，就没那么幸运了。说来复杂。

column5: I don't remember what my parents did, exactly.\nI think they owned some sort of tavern, or restaurant.\nIt's odd how I remember little else but the chaos.
column6: 我记不清父母具体是做什么的了。\n我想他们开过一家酒馆，或者餐馆。\n奇怪的是，我除了那场混乱，几乎什么都记不起来了。

column5: He slumps down in his chair, his posture emanating sorrow.
column6: 他瘫坐在椅子里，姿态中透着哀伤。

column5: I wouldn't normally tell anybody this, but you're special.\nOr — not really special, but you caught me holding onto it.
column6: 我一般不会跟任何人说这些，但你很特别。\n或者——也不算特别，只是被你撞见我在握着它。

column5: He holds out the brooch, and I get a clear look at it for the first time.{w}\nIt's a floral pattern, clearly feminine. I'm curious why he fancies it so much.
column6: 他递出那枚胸针，我第一次看清了它。{w}\n上面的花纹是花卉图案，明显是女式款。我好奇他为何如此钟爱它。

column5: This brooch? It used to belong to my Mother. She loved it.\nI made sure to retrieve it from her body after The Occupation.
column6: 这枚胸针？它曾属于我母亲。她很喜欢它。\n占领之后，我特意从她的遗体上取回了它。

column5: He scoffs, before shaking his head.
column6: 他嗤笑一声，摇了摇头。

column5: I remember the piles of bodies. Hundreds of them lining the town square.\nThe days after The Occupation were horrid. Corpses as far as the eye could see.\nLuckily, I knew exactly where they kept my Mother's body. So I went straight to it.
column6: 我记得那一堆堆的尸体。成百上千具排在镇广场上。\n占领后的那些日子很可怕。尸体一望无际。\n幸好，我清楚他们把我母亲的遗体放在了哪里。于是我径直去找它。

column5: How did I know...? Well, maybe I'll tell you another time.\nJust know that this brooch means more to me than anything else.\nWhen I hold onto it, it takes me back to simpler times, you know?
column6: 我怎么知道的……？嗯，也许改天再告诉你。\n你只要知道，这枚胸针对我来说比什么都重要。\n握着它的时候，它会带我回到更单纯的岁月，你懂吗？

column5: I don't tell anybody because they need me to be strong.\nYou can't win a war with sentiment, after all. \nI have a certain image to maintain.
column6: 我不告诉别人，因为他们需要我坚强。\n毕竟，靠多愁善感赢不了战争。\n我有特定的形象要维持。

column5: He looks at me with a smile.
column6: 他微笑着看我。

column5: But I feel like I can be myself around you.\nYou have the same burden — the same appearance to keep up.\nWhen we're together, I just feel like I can be myself.
column6: 但我觉得在你面前我可以做自己。\n你背负着同样的重担——也要维持同样的表象。\n我们在一起时，我就觉得能做回自己。

column5: Good, then it's settled.\nWe'll make sure to do this again.\nThere's plenty more to talk about.
column6: 好，那就这么定了。\n我们一定要再来一次。\n还有很多可聊的。

column5: Oh, uh — that caught me a little off guard.\nI guess it explains a few things. Honestly, I'm flattered.\nCan we please put a pin on that until next time...?
column6: 哦，呃——这让我有点措手不及。\n我想这解释了一些事。老实说，我受宠若惊。\n能不能先按下不表，留到下次……？

column5: That'll take a long time, I presume.\nBut it's all about the journey, isn't it?\nI'm sure we'll have a lot of fun along the way.
column6: 我想那会花很长时间。\n可重要的是过程，不是吗？\n我相信一路上我们会玩得很开心。

column5: If I had something to toast with, I'd agree.\nMaybe next time we can share a nice drink.\nI mean, hopefully this isn't the last time we do this.
column6: 要是有东西能碰杯，我就赞同了。\n也许下次我们可以好好喝一杯。\n我是说，但愿这不是我们最后一次这样。

column5: And sorry for venting about The Occupation.\nIt's not exactly the most cheery subject, right?\nJust felt right to open up to you some more.
column6: 还有，抱歉讲了那么多关于占领的事。\n那可不是什么愉快的话题，对吧？\n只是觉得该再对你敞开一些心扉。

column5: He stands up and pushes the chair back in.{w}\nI guess this was my signal to leave for now.{w}\nI stand up, and offer my hand for shaking.
column6: 他站起身，把椅子推回原位。{w}\n我想这就是让我暂且离开的信号。{w}\n我站起来，伸出手想和他握手。

column5: He does nothing, and I'm left looking like a fool.{w}\nThis isn't the first time he's refused to shake my hand.{w}\nRather than comment on the matter, he changes the subject.
column6: 他什么也没做，我倒显得像个傻瓜。{w}\n这已不是他第一次拒绝和我握手了。{w}\n他没就此事多言，而是换了个话题。

column5: Let's meet in the war room whenever you're ready, [firstname].\nThis might be your last resting day for a while, so spend it wisely.
column6: 你准备好了就到作战室来找我，[firstname]。\n这可能是你接下来一段时间里最后的休息日，好好珍惜。

column5: Let's meet in the war room whenever you're ready, [firstname].\nThis might be your last resting day for a while, so spend it wisely.
column6: 你准备好了就到作战室来找我，[firstname]。\n这可能是你接下来一段时间里最后的休息日，好好珍惜。

column5: He smirks, and sees me out of the room.{w}\nIt was nice to learn more about him, and his past.{w}\nRather than being the General, he's becoming more to me.
column6: 他微微一笑，送我出了房间。{w}\n能多了解他和他过去的事，真好。{w}\n对我而言，他不再只是那位将军了。

column5: He smirks, and sees me out of his room.{w}\nIt was nice to learn more about him, and his past.{w}\nRather than being the General, he's becoming a friend.
column6: 他微微一笑，送我出了他的房间。{w}\n能多了解他和他过去的事，真好。{w}\n他不再只是那位将军，而正成为朋友。

column5: I enter Howl's room, and I notice him standing with his back to me.{w}\nHe's in the corner of the room, with his hand pressed against the wall.{w}\nHe's mumbling to himself, and I do my best not to startle him at all.
column6: 我走进豪尔的房间，注意到他背对着我站着。{w}\n他在房间角落，一只手按在墙上。{w}\n他喃喃自语，我尽量不去惊动他。

column5: Bodies everywhere. Screams for help. Blood flowing.\nCorpses held tightly in their arms — they cry for the lost.\nBut the lost do not answer, for they have no voice.
column6: 到处都是尸体。求救的尖叫。血在流淌。\n他们怀里紧抱着尸体——为逝者痛哭。\n可逝者无法回应，因为他们已发不出声音。

column5: He feels shame, like he's responsible for all of this.\nBut soon after, he feels nothing at all. Until he rises again.\nVengeance controls his mind. It drives his clouded judgment.
column6: 他感到羞耻，仿佛这一切都是他的错。\n但不久之后，他就什么感觉都没有了。直到他再度站起。\n复仇掌控了他的心智。驱使着他被蒙蔽的判断。

column5: We see the future, as expected, but also the past.\nWe see your death, Monarch — even if it didn't happen.\nWhy does time play such tricks on our memories?
column6: 我们如预期般看见未来，但也看见了过去。\n君主，我们看见了你的死——即便它并未发生。\n时间为何要这样戏弄我们的记忆？

column5: He turns to face me. So he knew I was here all along.
column6: 他转身面向我。原来他一直都知道我在这儿。

column5: Are these memories, or perhaps echoes?\nThat is what I wished to talk to you about, Monarch.\nOur mind is overwhelmed, but not in the usual sense.
column6: 这些是记忆，还是某种回响？\n君主，这正是我想跟你谈的。\n我们的心智不堪重负，但不是通常意义上的那种。

column5: We expected you to say that. We've heard it before.\nIt's almost like you had no other choice. Interesting.\nThings are different now that we're free. So different.
column6: 我们料到你也会这么说。这话我们听过。\n就好像你别无选择。有意思。\n如今我们自由了，一切都不同了。截然不同。

column5: Exiting that prison has taken its toll on our minds.\nIn there, our sight was limited. But not anymore.\nInstead of just the future, we see everything.
column6: 离开那座牢笼，让我们的心智付出了代价。\n在那里，我们的视野受限。但如今不再如此。\n我们看见的不只是未来，而是一切。

column5: We see the past, and consequences of actions not taken.\nThe possibilities are infinite, and this is hard even to fathom.\nWe must narrow our vision. These details are unimportant.
column6: 我们看见过去，以及未曾采取的行动所带来的后果。\n可能性无穷无尽，这甚至难以理解。\n我们必须收窄视野。这些细节并不重要。

column5: We may not be of much use at the moment, Monarch.\nIt will take some time to adjust to these new circumstances.\nIf we choose to adjust, that is. Further evaluation is required.
column6: 君主，此刻我们或许帮不上什么忙。\n适应这些新境况需要一些时间。\n前提是我们选择去适应。还需进一步评估。

column5: We see a past where we failed to save you, Monarch.\nYou fell to your wounds, and Alestia had no hope at all.\nDamek, too. The failure of The Rebellion was certain.
column6: 君主，我们看见一个没能救下你的过去。\n你因伤倒下，阿莱斯蒂亚毫无希望。\n达梅克也是。反抗军的失败已成定局。

column5: Pirates rush to help, but not led by the same leader.\nUlric sacrificed himself to use the blade, and create an army.\nThe Monarch Vessels, or perhaps the Created Seers.
column6: 海盗们赶来相助，但领头人并非同一个。\n乌尔里克牺牲自己使用那把剑，创造出军队。\n君主容器，又或者是“造出来的先知”。

column5: Why do you say that seeing these things is important?\nIt is death, and carnage. The loss of all hope; and ultimately, death.\nOnly one thing remains constant in all of this. The Blade of Exodus.
column6: 你为什么说看见这些很重要？\n这是死亡与杀戮。是一切希望的破灭；最终，还是死亡。\n这一切之中唯一不变的，只有流亡之刃。

column5: We saw you say this as well. It led to ruin.\nOur culture was always focused on avoiding the wrong future.\nWe've never thought about seeing numerous versions of the past.
column6: 我们看见你也这么说。那通向毁灭。\n我们的文化向来专注于避开错误的未来。\n我们从未想过会看见过去的诸多版本。

column5: But we are sure that we see these things for a reason. \nPerhaps there is a secret to find, or a link hidden between them all.\nAs we travel, we will do our best to learn more about these visions.
column6: 但我们确信，看见这些必有其缘由。\n也许有个秘密待发掘，或者它们之间藏着某种联系。\n旅途中，我们会尽力多了解这些幻象。

column5: We simply wished to make you aware that they exist.\nIt is the opposite of everything we've ever encountered.\nBut at the end of the day, so are you. A huge anomaly.
column6: 我们只是希望让你知道它们的存在。\n这与我们历来所知的一切截然相反。\n但说到底，你也是这样。一个巨大的异数。

column5: I'm not sure what he means, since he speaks so cryptically.{w}\nBut he's having visions of different pasts — not just the future.{w}\nThat would be jarring to me as well. I only ever saw the future.
column6: 他说得如此隐晦，我不确定他是什么意思。{w}\n但他看见的是不同版本的过去——而不只是未来。{w}\n换作我也会不知所措。我向来只看见未来。

column5: But it was almost always a future that we wanted to avoid.{w}\nHow could you see a different past? That was always set in stone.{w}\nLet alone pasts so different as to detail the deaths of my comrades.
column6: 但那几乎总是我们想要避开的未来。{w}\n怎么可能看见不同的过去？过去向来是板上钉钉的。{w}\n更别说那些细致描述了同伴之死的、截然不同的过去。

column5: There had to be a reason — he was right.{w}\nBut it's unlikely that we'd find an answer anytime soon.{w}\nHe'd have to put up with this burden for a little bit longer.
column6: 一定有缘由——他说得对。{w}\n但短期内我们不太可能找到答案。{w}\n他只能再多背一阵子这份重担了。

column5: It pains us to see visions of your death, Monarch.\nFuture, or past — it is something we wish to avoid.\nYou carry our legacy. You are everything to us.
column6: 君主，看见你死亡的幻象让我们痛苦。\n无论未来还是过去——那都是我们想要避开的。\n你承载着我们的传承。你对我们而言就是一切。

column5: We request some time alone, if you'd give us the honor.\nWe will do our best to focus on more positive things.
column6: 若你肯赏脸，我们想独处一会儿。\n我们会尽力把注意力放在更积极的事情上。

column5: He turns back to the wall, and places his hand upon it.
column6: 他转回身面向墙壁，把手按了上去。

column5: Sharing an apple in a back alley. A growing bond.\nAlcohol brings forth childhood dreams. Dreams of change.\nYou grow close to a comrade despite their two-faced nature.
column6: 在后巷分享一个苹果。情谊渐长。\n酒精唤起童年的梦想。关于改变的梦想。\n尽管同伴两面三刀，你仍与他日渐亲近。

column5: A man seeks family to replace the one he never had.\nThere's a girl who finds the strength to succeed in her friends.\nWe wonder where we fit in amongst this group. We hope we can.
column6: 一个男人在寻找家人，以填补他从未拥有过的家。\n还有个女孩，从朋友身上找到了走向成功的勇气。\n我们好奇自己在这群人里该居于何处。但愿我们能融入。

column5: He looks down at the floor, and I take a few steps back.{w}\nFor now, it's probably best to leave him be. He seems overwhelmed.{w}\nIn his situation, I would be as well. He has to process a lot of new information.
column6: 他低头看着地板，我后退了几步。{w}\n眼下，最好还是别打扰他。他似乎被压得喘不过气。{w}\n换作是我也会如此。他得消化太多新信息。

column5: If I can find my place in all of this, so can he.{w}\nPerhaps we'd have more time to talk on the boat ride.
column6: 如果我能在这其中找到自己的位置，他也能。{w}\n也许坐船的路上我们有更多时间聊聊。

column5: I leave for the docks, confident to help him more in the future.
column6: 我动身前往码头，相信日后能更多地帮他。

column5: I enter the War Room, and see Damek standing over the table.{w}\nHe's moving wooden figures from place to place, forming a strategy.{w}\nI guess this was my first time seeing him in action. It was impressive.
column6: 我走进作战室，看见达梅克站在桌前。{w}\n他正把木制人偶从一个地方移到另一个地方，谋划着战略。{w}\n这该是我第一次看他运筹帷幄。真令人赞叹。

column5: I'm glad you came, [firstname].
column6: 很高兴你来了，[firstname]。

column5: I'm glad you came, [firstname].
column6: 很高兴你来了，[firstname]。

column5: He talks to me while he works, displaying grace and lack of effort.{w}\nIt's almost like this is second nature for him. What was he planning?{w}\nI notice a map on the table, with figures scattered about different regions.
column6: 他一边忙一边跟我说话，从容不迫，毫不费力。{w}\n这对他来说简直就像第二天性。他在谋划什么？{w}\n我注意到桌上有一张地图，人偶散布在各个区域上。

column5: So, tomorrow we'll begin your training with The Blade of Exodus.\nBut in addition to that, we'll have to train you in swordplay as well.\nI'll see if I can find someone left-handed to train you. It should work.
column6: 那么，明天我们就开始训练你使用流亡之刃。\n但除此之外，我们还得训练你的剑术。\n我看看能不能找个左撇子来教你。应该行得通。

column5: So, tomorrow we'll begin your training with The Blade of Exodus.\nBut in addition to that, we'll have to train you in swordplay as well.\nI think Ulric should be free. I can't really think of a better teacher.
column6: 那么，明天我们就开始训练你使用流亡之刃。\n但除此之外，我们还得训练你的剑术。\n我想乌尔里克应该有空。我想不出比他更好的老师了。

column5: He eyes the scabbard on my back, and the base of the sword.
column6: 他打量着我背上的剑鞘，还有剑柄底部。

column5: We think that the more you use it, the more you'll tolerate it.\nIf you're like me, you got overwhelmed the moment you touched it.\nIt's about adapting. Slow exposure will help you become stronger.
column6: 我们认为你用得越多，就越能耐受它。\n如果你和我一样，一碰到它就不堪重负。\n关键在于适应。慢慢接触会让你变得更强。

column5: But we're also in a rush, so I've worked out a schedule for you.\nIt balances both exposure therapy, as well as combat training.\nThere's a bit of free time in there, too. You'll be needing it.
column6: 但我们也很赶时间，所以我为你制定了一份日程。\n它兼顾了接触疗法和战斗训练。\n里面也留了点空闲时间。你会需要它的。

column5: He points to a paper resting on the war table.{w}\nI pick it up, and start to inspect the contents.{w}\nIt's a detailed itinerary. I'm impressed.
column6: 他指了指摊在作战桌上的一张纸。{w}\n我拿起来，开始细看上面的内容。{w}\n这是一份详细的日程安排。我很佩服。

column5: Now, there's one more thing.\nThe spirit idol we discovered is right down there.\nIt's a bit of a walk, so I'll have to show it to you later.
column6: 另外，还有一件事。\n我们发现的灵像就在那下面。\n路有点远，所以我得晚些再带你去看。

column5: He points to a small exit in the back corner of the room.{w}\nIt almost looks like the entrance of a cave. It stands out.{w}\nThey must've dug out a large portion of this room.
column6: 他指向房间后角落的一个小出口。{w}\n那几乎像个洞穴入口。显得很突兀。{w}\n他们一定把这个房间挖掉了很大一部分。

column5: It's also where I chose to bury Salus, our former leader.\nI guess I can be sentimental when it comes to that stuff.\nIt just seemed like the right thing to do, you know?
column6: 那也是我选择安葬萨卢斯的地方，我们的前任领袖。\n我想在这种事上我也会多愁善感。\n只是觉得那样做是对的，你懂吗？

column5: Now, let's go over your—
column6: 现在，我们来过一遍你的——

column5: Before he can continue, he's immediately cut off.{w}\nPro runs into the room, panting heavily, clearly exerted.{w}\nBut there's a hint of fright and concern on his face, too.
column6: 他还没说完，就立刻被打断了。{w}\n普洛跑进房间，喘着粗气，明显精疲力竭。{w}\n但他脸上也带着一丝惊恐与忧虑。

column5: Damek, come quick!
column6: 达梅克，快来！

column5: Pro...? What's going on?\nI'm in the middle of a meeting, here.
column6: 普洛……？怎么了？\n我这儿正开着会呢。

column5: The meeting can wait, Damek! Please!\nGryz is here, and he's causing a commotion!
column6: 会议可以等等，达梅克！求你了！\n格瑞兹来了，正在闹事！

column5: What!? Alright, let's go.\nWe should probably talk to him, [firstname].\nI'm pretty sure I know what he's after.
column6: 什么！？好吧，走。\n我们大概该去跟他谈谈，[firstname]。\n我很清楚他是冲着什么来的。

column5: What!? Alright, let's go.\nWe should probably talk to him, [firstname].\nI'm pretty sure I know what he's after.
column6: 什么！？好吧，走。\n我们大概该去跟他谈谈，[firstname]。\n我很清楚他是冲着什么来的。

column5: We all nod to one another, and Pro starts leading the way.{w}\nWhatever was coming our way, I'm sure Damek could handle it.
column6: 我们彼此点头示意，普洛开始带路。{w}\n无论前面等着我们的是什么，我相信达梅克都能应对。

column5: We run to the atrium to handle this situation as fast as we can.{w}\nWhen we arrive, I see Ulric standing imposingly before Gryz.{w}\nA good choice. Ulric could fight off almost anybody.
column6: 我们奔向中庭，尽快去处理这局面。{w}\n到了那里，我看见乌尔里克威风凛凛地站在格瑞兹面前。{w}\n选得好。乌尔里克几乎能击退任何人。

column5: Stand down, Gryz.
column6: 退下，格瑞兹。

column5: I only want to see Damek.\nWe had a deal, and it's {i}his{/i} turn to deliver.\nDon't forget, I'm the only reason you're down here.
column6: 我只想见达梅克。\n我们有约定，现在轮到他{i}兑现{/i}了。\n别忘了，你们能待在下面，全靠我。

column5: Hmph.
column6: 哼。

column5: Gryz looks back toward us, noticing our entrance.
column6: 格瑞兹回头看向我们，注意到我们进来了。

column5: Please Ulric, stand aside.\nInsubordination isn't your style.
column6: 拜托，乌尔里克，让开。\n抗命可不是你的风格。

column5: He tilts his head back toward Damek.{w}\nUlric turns and looks, noticing that we're here.{w}\nSaying nothing, he turns around and walks away.
column6: 他把头往后朝达梅克的方向一偏。{w}\n乌尔里克转头看去，注意到我们来了。{w}\n他一言不发，转身走开。

column5: He rests his back against the wall and simply watches.{w}\nIt seemed like almost all of the tension was cut from the air.{w}\nThose two men in deadlock was a scary sight to behold.
column6: 他背靠在墙上，只是旁观。{w}\n空气里的紧张似乎几乎一下子被抽空了。{w}\n那两人僵持的样子，看着真吓人。

column5: Good. Now, Damek — it's time.\nUnless anybody {i}else{/i} wants to challenge me?
column6: 很好。现在，达梅克——时候到了。\n除非还有{i}别的{/i}人想挑战我？

column5: Damek takes slow steps forward, cautious not to make sudden movements.{w}\nGryz grips the handle of the hammer resting on his back, as if to threaten.
column6: 达梅克缓缓向前迈步，小心翼翼不做出突然的动作。{w}\n格瑞兹握住背在身后的锤柄，仿佛在威胁。

column5: Now now, Gryz — let's remain calm.\nI fully intend to hold up my end of the bargain.\nThere was just some important business to take care of.
column6: 好了好了，格瑞兹——我们冷静点。\n我完全打算履行我这边的约定。\n只是有些重要的事务要处理。

column5: He motions toward me.
column6: 他朝我示意。

column5: Yeah, I know.\nBut all the pieces are in place, Damek.\nWill you {i}please{/i} take me to see it?
column6: 是啊，我知道。\n但所有条件都已齐备，达梅克。\n你{i}能不能{/i}带我去看看它？

column5: Damek shuffles in place, anxious.
column6: 达梅克原地挪动着脚步，显得焦虑。

column5: I suppose I can rearrange my schedule a {i}bit{/i}.\nSorry if it appeared like I was going back on my word.
column6: 我想我可以把日程{i}稍微{/i}调整一下。\n如果看起来像是我要食言，抱歉。

column5: I'll accept that apology when you take me to the idol.\nI'm sure you understand. I'm past the point of buying time.\nAnd make sure you bring that new friend of yours, as well.
column6: 等你带我去看灵像，我再接受你的道歉。\n你肯定明白。我已经过了可以被拖延的时候了。\n还有，记得把你那位新朋友也带上。

column5: Oh, so it was the idol he wanted...?{w}\nAnd from the way he spoke, he wanted me as well.{w}\nOf course, this is all likely related to The Blade of Exodus.
column6: 哦，原来他想要的是灵像……？{w}\n从他说话的方式看，他也想要我。{w}\n当然，这一切多半都和流亡之刃有关。

column5: Very well.
column6: 很好。

column5: Damek simply concedes without contest.{w}\nOf course, before we can move, there's an interruption.{w}\nBeing a Rebel was a busy life. It's always something.
column6: 达梅克毫不争辩地让步了。{w}\n当然，我们还没动身，就被打断了。{w}\n当反抗军的日子很忙。总有事情冒出来。

column5: However, this something was far bigger than any of us imagined.{w}\nDamek looks on in shock as a young man slowly enters the room.{w}\nWith heavy, labored steps, they appear to be weak and tired.
column6: 然而，这件事比我们任何人想象的都要重大。{w}\n达梅克震惊地看着一个年轻人慢慢走进房间。{w}\n他的步伐沉重费力，显得虚弱而疲惫。

column5: Shane...?\nShane, you're back!
column6: 肖恩……？\n肖恩，你回来了！

column5: Damek runs forward, and Gryz steps back.{w}\nHe seems to understand what was going on, too.{w}\nShane had come back from his trip to Balteus?
column6: 达梅克冲上前，格瑞兹退后一步。{w}\n他似乎也明白发生了什么。{w}\n肖恩从巴尔泰乌斯之行回来了？

column5: Damek...
column6: 达梅克……

column5: Shane, I can't believe this.\nI was so worried that we lost you.
column6: 肖恩，我真不敢相信。\n我一直担心我们失去了你。

column5: Everyone watches in awe.
column6: 所有人都敬畏地注视着。

column5: Did they hurt you...?\nAre you okay? Do you need anything?\nPro, go grab some water, quick...!
column6: 他们伤到你了吗……？\n你还好吗？需要什么吗？\n普洛，快去拿点水……！

column5: No, Damek. I'm fine.\nDon't worry about it, Pro.
column6: 不用了，达梅克。我没事。\n别忙了，普洛。

column5: Pro stops in his tracks upon hearing this.{w}\nIf anything, it just looked like Shane needed some rest.
column6: 普洛听到这话，停住了脚步。{w}\n要说的话，肖恩看起来只是需要休息。

column5: I'm sorry, Damek...
column6: 对不起，达梅克……

column5: For what...? Don't be silly, Shane.\nI'm the one who should be apologizing, here.\nIt was foolish of me to send you into danger like that!
column6: 对不起什么……？别傻了，肖恩。\n该道歉的人是我。\n把你送进那样的险境，是我太愚蠢了！

column5: Shane steps forward, and wraps his arms around Damek.{w}\nEveryone seems so relieved, and all of the tension is gone.{w}\nEven Gryz cracks a smile as he watches this happy reunion.
column6: 肖恩上前一步，一把抱住达梅克。{w}\n所有人都像是松了口气，紧张的气氛一扫而空。{w}\n就连格瑞兹看着这场重逢，也露出了笑容。

column5: But Shane takes advantage of our lowered guard.{w}\nReaching into his pocket, he pulls out a dagger.{w}\nBefore any of us can react, the damage is done.
column6: 但肖恩利用了我们松懈的防备。{w}\n他从口袋里抽出一把匕首。{w}\n我们还没来得及反应，伤害已经造成。

column5: Damek screams, and stumbles back in shock.{w}\nShane was fast. His abdomen is {i}covered{/i} in wounds.{w}\nHe shakes, blood spilling on the floor at an alarming rate.
column6: 达梅克尖叫一声，震惊地向后退去。{w}\n肖恩出手太快了。他的腹部{i}布满{/i}伤口。{w}\n他颤抖着，鲜血以惊人的速度溅落在地。

column5: Shane...?
column6: 肖恩……？

column5: Ulric is the first to react, and he tries to restrain Shane.{w}\nHowever, it's no use. He's far too agile to be caught.
column6: 乌尔里克最先反应过来，试图制服肖恩。{w}\n然而无济于事。他太敏捷了，根本抓不住。

column5: Shane, what have you done!?
column6: 肖恩，你干了什么！？

column5: He doesn't respond, and grabs a bow and some arrows from a nearby weapon stand.{w}\nAll of us are panicking, not sure what to do. Could Ulric take on Shane alone...?
column6: 他没有回应，从旁边的武器架上抓起一把弓和几支箭。{w}\n我们都慌了神，不知如何是好。乌尔里克能独自对付肖恩吗……？

column5: Within a few moments, though, that is the absolute least of our worries.
column6: 可没过一会儿，那已是最微不足道的担忧了。

column5: Sovy — now!
column6: 索维——就是现在！

column5: Immediately after, Sovy enters the room from the entrance to the tunnels.{w}\nThere's a man in a white suit of armor with him, too. Like the Honor Guard.{w}\nWhat was he doing here...? This was definitely coordinated. We're in trouble.
column6: 紧接着，索维从通往隧道的入口走进房间。{w}\n他身边还有个穿白色盔甲的男人，像是荣誉卫队。{w}\n他来这里做什么……？这绝对是早有预谋。我们有麻烦了。

column5: Sometimes I wish it wouldn't be so easy.\nLook Halin, even the suits of armor are still alive.\nAll the time in the world, and they didn't even act.
column6: 有时我倒希望它别这么容易。\n看啊，哈林，连那些盔甲都还活着。\n明明有那么多时间，它们却毫无反应。

column5: Pitiful.
column6: 可悲。

column5: They both look at all of the Honor Guard in the atrium.{w}\nMinding their own business, they just stumble around.{w}\nThere's a lot, but they posed no real threat to anybody.
column6: 两人望向中庭里所有的荣誉卫队。{w}\n它们自顾自地蹒跚游荡。{w}\n数量不少，却对任何人都构不成真正的威胁。

column5: Sovy steps forward, looking at all of us.{w}\nUlric grips his blade, and stands in the way.
column6: 索维上前一步，扫视着我们所有人。{w}\n乌尔里克紧握刀刃，挡在路中。

column5: Leave.
column6: 滚开。

column5: Or else what?
column6: 不然怎样？

column5: I'll {i}kill{/i} you.
column6: 我就{i}杀了{/i}你。

column5: So dramatic, Ulric. You've certainly grown.\nWhere was {i}that{/i} bravado five-hundred years ago...?
column6: 真会演，乌尔里克。你确实长大了。\n五百年前，{i}那股{/i}豪气又去哪儿了……？

column5: Ulric growls and grits his teeth, easily provoked.{w}\nAll of us are locked in place, too scared to move.
column6: 乌尔里克低吼着咬紧牙关，一点就着。{w}\n我们都僵在原地，吓得动弹不得。

column5: You're outnumbered. Don't test me.\nIf Damek dies, we'll find another leader.\nYou've done no real damage to us, Sovy.
column6: 你们寡不敌众。别逼我。\n就算达梅克死了，我们也会另找一位领袖。\n你并没有给我们造成真正的损失，索维。

column5: Is that so...?
column6: 是吗……？

column5: Sovy grins, and raises one of his hands in the air.{w}\nWith a dramatic snap of his fingers, I stumble back.{w}\nThe blade is reacting, and trembling. What's going on...!?
column6: 索维咧嘴一笑，抬起一只手。{w}\n随着他夸张地一个响指，我踉跄后退。{w}\n那把剑在反应，在颤抖。怎么回事……！？

column5: There's a quick flash of white light. Wait — I know this feeling.{w}\nFrom my vision of Valinorth, when he animated those suits of armor...{w}\nCan he truly manipulate the blade without even touching it?
column6: 一道白光骤然闪过。等等——我认得这种感觉。{w}\n在我关于瓦利诺斯的幻象里，当他让那些盔甲动起来时……{w}\n他真的能不碰那把剑就操纵它吗？

column5: He can...
column6: 他能……

column5: All hell breaks loose before I can even start to process these events.{w}\nThe Honor Guard grab their blades and start massacring the rebels.{w}\nWith a simple snap of his fingers, he sent them all into a murderous rage.
column6: 我还没来得及理清这些事，一切就已乱作一团。{w}\n荣誉卫队抄起刀刃，开始屠戮反抗军。{w}\n仅仅一个响指，他就让它们全都陷入了杀戮的狂怒。

column5: All I can hear is screams of agony as our forces are caught off guard.{w}\nBodies start to litter the floor, while other Rebels grab weapons and fight.{w}\nGryz runs forward, and grabs Damek's body, slowly dragging it away.
column6: 我方措手不及时，我所能听到的只有痛苦的惨叫。{w}\n尸体开始横陈一地，另有反抗军抓起武器抵抗。{w}\n格瑞兹冲上前，抱起达梅克的身体，缓缓将它拖走。

column5: [firstname], come with me!\nLet the Rebels keep the enemy occupied!\nI have an idea, but you need to do what I say!
column6: [firstname]，跟我来！\n让反抗军拖住敌人！\n我有个主意，但你得照我说的做！

column5: [firstname], come with me!\nLet the Rebels keep the enemy occupied!\nI have an idea, but you need to do what I say!
column6: [firstname]，跟我来！\n让反抗军拖住敌人！\n我有个主意，但你得照我说的做！

column5: I nod, and follow after him.{w}\nI'm still not able to process {i}anything{/i}.{w}\nHow would The Rebellion recover from this?
column6: 我点点头，跟在他身后。{w}\n我依然什么{i}都无法{/i}理清。{w}\n反抗军要如何从这场灾难中恢复？

column5: Within minutes, almost all of the Rebels were killed.{w}\nThis isn't how things were supposed to happen...!
column6: 短短几分钟，几乎所有反抗军都被杀死了。{w}\n事情不该是这样的……！

column5: I look down at Damek's body, and it's motionless.{w}\nA trail of blood follows me and Gryz as we flee the area.{w}\nBut before we can leave the atrium, Shane notices the trail.
column6: 我低头看向达梅克的身体，它一动不动。{w}\n我和格瑞兹逃离时，身后留下一道血痕。{w}\n可我们还没离开中庭，肖恩就注意到了那道血痕。

column5: I feel a sharp pain in my chest, and suddenly drop to the floor.{w}\nI can't move. I look down and notice an arrowhead protruding from my torso.{w}\nHe shot me in the back. That's all I can take in before everything fades away.
column6: 我感到胸口一阵剧痛，随即倒在地上。{w}\n我动不了。我低头看去，发现一支箭头从我躯干上凸出来。{w}\n他射中了我的背。这是我意识消散前唯一能接收到的事。

column5: However, with what just happened — I'm certain of one simple fact.
column6: 然而，就凭刚刚发生的一切——我确信一个简单的事实。

column5: The Rebellion is no more...
column6: 反抗军已经不复存在了……

column5: Valessa and Fortaime rush to the atrium, frightened by the sound of commotion.{w}\nMembers of the Honor Guard rush past them — to carry out their brutal objective.{w}\nWhen they arrive, a horror awaits them. It's clear that The Rebellion has lost.
column6: 瓦莱莎和福泰姆被骚动的声响惊到，赶向中庭。{w}\n荣誉卫队的成员从他们身旁冲过——去执行它们残忍的任务。{w}\n当他们抵达时，眼前一片惨状。反抗军显然已经败了。

column5: Oh no...
column6: 哦，不……

column5: Ulric, what's going on!?
column6: 乌尔里克，发生什么了！？

column5: Ulric is locked in combat with Sovy, violently swinging his sword.{w}\nBut Sovy dodges with ease, swaying his body from side to side.{w}\nWhen he gets a chance, he lands a harsh punch on Ulric's chest.
column6: 乌尔里克与索维激战，猛烈挥剑。{w}\n可索维轻松躲闪，身体左右摇摆。{w}\n一有机会，他就重重一拳打在乌尔里克胸口。

column5: Falling back, Ulric is brought to his knees.{w}\nHe pants heavily, trembling as he rises back up.
column6: 乌尔里克向后倒下，跪倒在地。{w}\n他大口喘气，颤抖着站起身来。

column5: I don't hide behind a sword like you and your Seer.\nNow tell me Ulric, how does it feel to lose to me...?\nTo see everything around you crumble and fall.
column6: 我可不像你和你的先知那样躲在剑后面。\n现在告诉我，乌尔里克，输给我是什么感觉……？\n眼看着周围的一切崩塌陷落。

column5: I don't hide behind a sword like you and your Seeress.\nNow tell me Ulric, how does it feel to lose to me...?\nTo see everything around you crumble and fall.
column6: 我可不像你和你的先知那样躲在剑后面。\n现在告诉我，乌尔里克，输给我是什么感觉……？\n眼看着周围的一切崩塌陷落。

column5: He laughs — that maniacal cackle echoing through the halls.
column6: 他大笑起来——那疯狂的笑声在大厅中回荡。

column5: Perhaps now you regret changing sides?
column6: 也许现在你后悔倒戈了？

column5: Never. This isn't over, Sovy.\nStand back, both of you!
column6: 绝不。这事还没完，索维。\n你们两个，退后！

column5: He waves his arm dismissively at Valessa and Fortaime.{w}\nHowever, it was already too late. The Honor Guard is closing in on them.{w}\nUlric turns and tries to help them, but a blow to the back of his head knocks him down.
column6: 他冲瓦莱莎和福泰姆不耐烦地摆了摆手。{w}\n然而已经太迟了。荣誉卫队正逼近他们。{w}\n乌尔里克转身想帮他们，可后脑挨了一记重击，被打倒在地。

column5: He can only watch through blurred vision as the Honor Guard overpowers them.{w}\nScreams assault his ears, and they're slowly silenced. Had they been killed, too...?{w}\nHe scans the room, trying to find Pro, but he can't. Perhaps he's among the bodies.
column6: 他只能透过模糊的视线，看着荣誉卫队将他们制服。{w}\n惨叫声刺入他的耳朵，而后渐渐沉寂。他们也死了吗……？{w}\n他扫视房间，想找到普洛，却找不到。也许他也在那些尸体之中。

column5: Sovy steps over and kicks Ulric in the gut, causing him to grunt and roll over.{w}\nA few moments later, he kneels down, and stares Ulric straight in the eyes.
column6: 索维跨步上前，一脚踹在乌尔里克腹部，让他闷哼一声翻了身。{w}\n片刻后，他跪下来，直视乌尔里克的眼睛。

column5: You thought you had everything under control.\nAbandon Valinorth — gather your forces — and attack Balteus?\nIt would work, if we didn't have you in our grip the entire time.
column6: 你以为一切都在你掌控之中。\n放弃瓦利诺斯——集结兵力——然后攻打巴尔泰乌斯？\n要不是我们始终攥着你们，这倒真能奏效。

column5: All we wanted was to destroy Mazeo's spirit idol, Ulric.\nThe final idol in all of Alestia. The sickness — almost cured.\nI know what you're thinking, though. The vision of Valinorth?
column6: 我们想要的只是毁掉马泽奥的灵像，乌尔里克。\n阿莱斯蒂亚全境的最后一座灵像。这顽疾——几乎就要治愈了。\n不过我知道你在想什么。瓦利诺斯的幻象？

column5: The Seer saw only what The Triumvirate wanted him to see.\nA trick — to lure every single one of you down here. It worked.\nAnd after I kill you, The Seer's life and that blade will be {i}mine{/i}.
column6: 先知看到的，只是三人执政团想让他看到的。\n一个圈套——把你们每一个人都引到下面来。它奏效了。\n等我杀了你，先知的生命和那把剑就都归{i}我{/i}了。

column5: The Seeress saw only what The Triumvirate wanted her to see.\nA trick — to lure every single one of you down here. It worked.\nAnd after I kill you, The Seeress' life and that blade will be {i}mine{/i}.
column6: 先知看到的，只是三人执政团想让他看到的。\n一个圈套——把你们每一个人都引到下面来。它奏效了。\n等我杀了你，先知的生命和那把剑就都归{i}我{/i}了。

column5: May The Triumvirate reign eternal...
column6: 愿三人执政团永世长存……

column5: Shane and Halin approach Sovy, leaving Ulric to look up at all three.{w}\nSovy holds a hand out to Shane, who gives him his dagger without hesitation.{w}\nPressing it up against Ulric's throat, Sovy pauses, savoring the fear in his eyes.
column6: 肖恩和哈林走近索维，留下乌尔里克仰望着他们三人。{w}\n索维向肖恩伸出手，肖恩毫不犹豫地把匕首递给他。{w}\n索维把匕首抵在乌尔里克喉头，顿了顿，品味着他眼中的恐惧。

column5: I'd ask if you had any last words...\nBut you don't deserve the satisfaction.
column6: 我本想问你是否还有遗言……\n但你不配得到这份满足。

column5: Not so fast...!
column6: 别急……！

column5: Everybody quickly turns to look as Pro runs in from the tunnels.{w}\nHe pants heavily, having clearly run a large amount. He smirks.
column6: 普洛从隧道里跑进来，所有人都立刻转头看去。{w}\n他喘得厉害，显然跑了很长的路。他咧嘴一笑。

column5: Nada, do it now!
column6: 娜达，动手！

column5: Alex, do it now!
column6: 亚历克斯，动手！

column5: A few moments later, an army of pirates floods in from the tunnels.{w}\nSovy, Halin and Shane quickly become defensive, trying to fend them off.{w}\nThere was enough now that they stood a chance. Their targets were clear.
column6: 片刻之后，一支海盗大军从隧道涌了进来。{w}\n索维、哈林和肖恩立刻转入守势，试图抵挡。{w}\n如今人数够了，他们有了胜算。目标也很明确。

column5: Using the commotion as cover, Pro rushes to Ulric's side.{w}\nHe helps him get on his feet, as he finally returns to his senses.
column6: 普洛借着混乱作掩护，冲到乌尔里克身边。{w}\n他扶他站起来，乌尔里克终于回过神来。

column5: Where is everybody else...?\nValessa, Fortaime, The Seer...?
column6: 其他人都去哪儿了……？\n瓦莱莎、福泰姆、先知……？

column5: Where is everybody else...?\nValessa, Fortaime, The Seeress...?
column6: 其他人都去哪儿了……？\n瓦莱莎、福泰姆、先知……？

column5: Ulric looks down at the floor, ashamed.
column6: 乌尔里克羞愧地低头看着地板。

column5: It's too late.
column6: 太迟了。

column5: He places a hand on Ulric's shoulder.{w}\nShaking his head, he knows that Ulric is wrong.
column6: 他把一只手搭在乌尔里克肩上。{w}\n他摇摇头，知道乌尔里克说错了。

column5: It's never too late.\nCome on, let's take them down.\nThey won't get away with this. They can't.
column6: 永远都不算太迟。\n来吧，我们把他们干掉。\n他们别想就这样蒙混过去。绝不能。

column5: Ulric smiles and nods, and they quickly rush into combat.{w}\nThings were starting to turn around. They were no longer outnumbered.{w}\nSovy, however, uses this commotion to sneak deeper underground.
column6: 乌尔里克笑着点点头，他们立刻投入战斗。{w}\n局势开始逆转。他们不再寡不敌众。{w}\n然而索维借着这片混乱，悄悄潜往地下更深处。

column5: While everyone was distracted — his objective was clear.
column6: 趁所有人都分神之际——他的目标很明确。

column5: Gryz carries me and Damek into the room behind the war table.{w}\nThe massive spirit idol glows, and radiates energy. It's beautiful.{w}\nThrough my faded vision, it only appears more surreal and odd.
column6: 格瑞兹把我和达梅克抱进作战桌后面的房间。{w}\n那巨大的灵像发光，散发着能量。很美。{w}\n在我模糊的视野里，它只显得更加超现实而诡异。

column5: He carries me to one side of the room and rests me down.{w}\nI notice that the arrow in my chest is gone, replaced with bloodied wrappings.{w}\nHe must've treated me during the time I just lost. But what about Damek...?
column6: 他把我抱到房间一侧，让我躺下。{w}\n我注意到胸口的箭不见了，取而代之的是沾血的绷带。{w}\n在我刚失去意识的那段时间里，他一定替我处理过了。可达梅克呢……？

column5: There were some supplies back in the crew quarters.\nI was able to treat your wound — no vital areas were harmed.\nIt's almost like he did that on purpose. Unless you got {i}really{/i} lucky.
column6: 船员舱里还有些补给。\n我总算处理了你的伤口——没伤到要害。\n简直像是他故意这么做的。除非你{i}真的{/i}命大。

column5: He sighs and looks back at Damek, who he had rested down on the other side.
column6: 他叹了口气，回头看向被他安置在另一侧的达梅克。

column5: But he {i}wasn't{/i} lucky.\nI'm sorry, Seer. He's gone.
column6: 可他{i}没有{/i}那么幸运。\n对不起，先知。他走了。

column5: But he {i}wasn't{/i} lucky.\nI'm sorry, Seeress. He's gone.
column6: 可他{i}没有{/i}那么幸运。\n对不起，先知。他走了。

column5: No...
But we can still fix this.\nThis is what I've been wanting all along.\nA chance to tap into that idol's power.
column6: 但我们还能挽回。\n这正是我一直想要的。\n一个借用那灵像力量的机会。

column5: He looks at the blade on my back.{w}\nReaching behind my shoulder, he undoes the scabbard.{w}\nIt falls to the ground. He closes his eyes and takes a deep breath.
column6: 他看着我背上的剑。{w}\n他探手到我肩后，解开剑鞘。{w}\n剑鞘落到地上。他闭上眼，深吸一口气。

column5: Please, let me take your blade.\nThis is the deal I made with Damek.\nTo free the spirits from those suits of armor.
column6: 求你，让我拿走你的剑。\n这是我和达梅克定下的交易。\n把那些灵从盔甲中解放出来。

column5: I look up at him, confused.{w}\nPain courses through my body, and I tremble.{w}\nI grab the scabbard, and hold it tightly in my hands.
column6: 我困惑地抬头看他。{w}\n疼痛传遍全身，我颤抖着。{w}\n我抓住剑鞘，紧紧握在手里。

column5: Please, [firstname]. There isn't much time.\nTwenty years ago — I led The Occupation with Sovy.\nThe people I killed. They're trapped in those suits of armor.
column6: 求你，[firstname]。时间不多了。\n二十年前——我和索维一起领导了那场占领。\n被我杀死的人。他们都困在那些盔甲里。

column5: Please, [firstname]. There isn't much time.\nTwenty years ago — I led The Occupation with Sovy.\nThe people I killed. They're trapped in those suits of armor.
column6: 求你，[firstname]。时间不多了。\n二十年前——我和索维一起领导了那场占领。\n被我杀死的人。他们都困在那些盔甲里。

column5: If you give me the blade, I can use the power of that idol.\nI'll release those spirits. I'll give them the freedom they deserve.\nI {i}need{/i} to do this. It's the only way I can make up for what I did!
column6: 如果你把剑给我，我就能借助那灵像的力量。\n我会释放那些灵。还给他们应得的自由。\n我{i}必须{/i}这么做。这是我唯一能弥补过错的方式！

column5: And without The Honor Guard, this battle is won.\nYour allies can easily fight against Sovy and his men.\nThere's still a chance to win, here. We {i}need{/i} to take it.
column6: 而且没有了荣誉卫队，这场仗就赢了。\n你的盟友们能轻松对付索维和他的人。\n这里还有翻盘的机会。我们{i}必须{/i}抓住它。

column5: He looks down at the floor, and his ears fall flat.
column6: 他低头看着地板，耳朵也垂了下来。

column5: I know why I recognized you and your friends back at my office.\nDuring The Occupation, there were people that looked just like you.\nI was just following orders. Trust me, I regret what I did. All of it.
column6: 我知道为什么当初在我的办公室，我会认出你和你的朋友。\n占领期间，有和你长得一模一样的人。\n我只是在执行命令。相信我，我后悔自己的所作所为。全部。

column5: Wait...? Does he mean...?
column6: 等等……？他是指……？

column5: Your parents. They were in Mazeo during The Occupation, right?\nIt's more than coincidence. This must be happening for a reason.\nThey aren't dead, Seer. They're trapped in those suits of armor.
column6: 你的父母。占领期间他们就在马泽奥，对吧？\n这绝不只是巧合。这一切发生必有其缘由。\n他们没有死，先知。他们被困在那些盔甲里。

column5: Your parents. They were in Mazeo during The Occupation, right?\nIt's more than coincidence. This must be happening for a reason.\nThey aren't dead, Seeress. They're trapped in those suits of armor.
column6: 你的父母。占领期间他们就在马泽奥，对吧？\n这绝不只是巧合。这一切发生必有其缘由。\n他们没有死，先知。他们被困在那些盔甲里。

column5: I notice the glisten of tears forming in his eyes.
column6: 我注意到他眼里泛起泪光。

column5: Sent there by me...
column6: 是我把他们派去的……

column5: Let me free them, Seer.\nIt's what they would want.\nIt's what they {i}all{/i} want.
column6: 让我解放他们，先知。\n这是他们的心愿。\n这是他们{i}所有人{/i}的心愿。

column5: Let me free them, Seeress.\nIt's what they would want.\nIt's what they {i}all{/i} want.
column6: 让我解放他们，先知。\n这是他们的心愿。\n这是他们{i}所有人{/i}的心愿。

column5: My grip on the scabbard tightens. He killed our parents...?{w}\nI can tell he's truly sorry, but this is just too much to take in.{w}\nThe pain in my chest gets more intense, and I wince.
column6: 我握剑鞘的手更紧了。他杀了我们的父母……？{w}\n我看得出他是真心悔恨，可这实在让人难以接受。{w}\n胸口的疼痛愈发剧烈，我不禁蹙眉。

column5: Here, I've got you.
column6: 来，我扶着你。

column5: He wraps one arm around me, slowly helping me to my feet.{w}\nTogether, we take slow steps across the room, toward the idol.{w}\nI look at Damek's body in the corner of my eye. Still, and lifeless.
column6: 他一只手臂环住我，慢慢把我扶起来。{w}\n我们一起缓缓穿过房间，朝灵像走去。{w}\n我余光瞥见达梅克的身体。静止，毫无生气。

column5: I stopped serving The Triumvirate the moment I got the chance.\nBeing forced to live in those suits? Forced to wear their colors?\nNobody should have to suffer such a fate. We can {i}fix{/i} this.
column6: 我一有机会就不再为三人执政团效力了。\n被迫活在那些盔甲里？被迫披着他们的颜色？\n没人该遭受这样的命运。我们能{i}纠正{/i}这一切。

column5: As we get closer to the idol, the earth starts to shake.{w}\nThere's a massive reaction coming from my blade.{w}\nGryz holds me tighter, as the tremors get more intense.
column6: 我们越靠近灵像，大地便开始震颤。{w}\n我的剑迸发出巨大的反应。{w}\n震动愈发剧烈，格瑞兹把我抱得更紧。

column5: I picked up some information when I served The Triumvirate.\nThat blade has the ability to bend its power to your will.\nIt all depends on what the wielder wants it to do.
column6: 我为三人执政团效力时，打探到了一些情报。\n那把剑能将它的力量屈从于持剑者的意志。\n一切取决于持剑者想让它做什么。

column5: They want power, and so it gives them an army.\nWe want freedom — so that's what we'll have.\nPlease, Seer. Let me do this. It's all I ask.
column6: 他们渴求权力，于是它给他们一支军队。\n我们渴求自由——那我们就会得到自由。\n求你，先知。让我来做这件事。我只求这个。

column5: They want power, and so it gives them an army.\nWe want freedom — so that's what we'll have.\nPlease, Seeress. Let me do this. It's all I ask.
column6: 他们渴求权力，于是它给他们一支军队。\n我们渴求自由——那我们就会得到自由。\n求你，先知。让我来做这件事。我只求这个。

column5: Each step we take causes emotion to well up within me.{w}\nThis is all too much — it's all happening too fast.{w}\nNo matter how hard I think, I have no idea what to do.
column6: 我们每走一步，我心中的情绪就翻涌得更厉害。{w}\n这一切太过沉重——发生得太快了。{w}\n无论我如何苦思，都不知道该怎么做。

column5: I know it will kill me, but I've come to terms with that.\nIt's a fitting punishment, considering what I've done.
column6: 我知道这会要了我的命，但我已坦然接受。\n以我所做之事而言，这是应得的惩罚。

column5: We reach the idol, and I'm almost blinded by its light.{w}\nI can understand that Gryz wants his redemption, but...{w}\nHis crimes against the world, and our families, were awful.
column6: 我们走到灵像前，它的光芒几乎刺得我睁不开眼。{w}\n我能理解格瑞兹想要救赎，可是……{w}\n他对这个世界、对我们的家人犯下的罪行，太可怕了。

column5: I could always tap into the power of this idol myself.{w}\nHow would Valessa and Fortaime feel if I sided with Gryz?{w}\nSome crimes aren't forgivable. Is this one of them...?
column6: 我本也可以亲自借用这灵像的力量。{w}\n要是我站在格瑞兹这边，瓦莱莎和福泰姆会怎么想？{w}\n有些罪行不可饶恕。这算其中之一吗……？

column5: Please...
column6: 求你了……

column5: I suppose it was. He truly felt bad for his actions in the past.{w}\nWith a slight nod, I hand him the scabbard, and he smiles.
column6: 我想是的吧。他确实为自己过去的行为深感愧疚。{w}\n我微微点头，把剑鞘交给他，他笑了。

column5: Thank you, [firstname].\nStand back. This could get dangerous.
column6: 谢谢你，[firstname]。\n退后。这可能会很危险。

column5: Thank you, [firstname].\nStand back. This could get dangerous.
column6: 谢谢你，[firstname]。\n退后。这可能会很危险。

column5: Doing as instructed, I stand there and watch him act.{w}\nI need to back against the wall, since the pain is still so intense.{w}\nWithout spiritual energy inside of him, the blade would kill him quickly.
column6: 我遵照吩咐，站在那里看着他行动。{w}\n疼痛依旧剧烈，我不得不靠到墙上。{w}\n他体内没有灵能量，那把剑很快就会要了他的命。

column5: I'm glad that he thought it was a worthy sacrifice.{w}\nFreeing the spirits, and destroying The Honor Guard in the tunnels?{w}\nThe tables would be easily turned. We'd come back from this defeat!
column6: 我很庆幸他认为这是值得的牺牲。{w}\n解放那些灵，并摧毁隧道里的荣誉卫队？{w}\n局势将轻易逆转。我们会从这场惨败中东山再起！

column5: He hesitates.
column6: 他犹豫了。

column5: So, I guess this is it.
column6: 那么，我想就是现在了。

column5: He closes his eyes.
column6: 他闭上了眼睛。

column5: I'm sorry, everybody...\nI hope you can learn to forgive me.\nIn your final moments, {i}know{/i} The Triumvirate will fall.
column6: 对不起，各位……\n希望你们能学会原谅我。\n在你们最后的时刻，请{i}相信{/i}三人执政团终将覆灭。

column5: I see him take the blade out of the scabbard.{w}\nBut after that, I see only white. That blinding light.{w}\nGryz grunts, clearly overpowered by the blade.
column6: 我看见他把剑从鞘中抽出。{w}\n可之后，我只看到一片白。那刺目的光。{w}\n格瑞兹闷哼一声，显然被那把剑压制住了。

column5: The ground begins to shake even more.{w}\nIt's worrisome, since we're in a cavern.{w}\nIf it caved in — that would be the end.
column6: 地面震动得更厉害了。{w}\n我们身处洞穴之中，这令人担忧。{w}\n要是它塌了——那就全完了。

column5: You're free now...\nAnd so am I...
column6: 你们自由了……\n我也自由了……

column5: The light slowly subsides, and my eyes start to adjust.{w}\nWhen they do, I see Gryz dead on the ground, clutching the blade.{w}\nThe idol starts to flicker, its light slowly going dim. Was it over...?
column6: 光芒渐渐消退，我的眼睛开始适应。{w}\n等我看清时，只见格瑞兹倒在地上，紧握着那把剑，已经死了。{w}\n灵像开始闪烁，光芒缓缓变暗。结束了吗……？

column5: I slowly walk over to him, but the tremors continue.{w}\nWith a violent shake, I'm thrown on the floor.{w}\nCrawling over, I do my best to reach the blade.
column6: 我慢慢走向他，可震动仍在继续。{w}\n一阵猛烈的摇晃把我掀倒在地。{w}\n我爬过去，尽力去够那把剑。

column5: Would The Honor Guard fall...?{w}\nWas this truly the end of this nightmare?{w}\nI hope that's the case, as I arrive at the blade.
column6: 荣誉卫队会倒下吗……？{w}\n这场噩梦真的结束了吗？{w}\n我爬到剑边时，满心希望正是如此。

column5: Stabbing it into the ground, I slowly use it to help myself up.{w}\nIt's hard because of the tremors, and I almost lose my balance.{w}\nBut with enough effort and strength, I'm finally back on my feet.
column6: 我把剑插进地里，慢慢撑着站起来。{w}\n因为震动，这很难，我差点失去平衡。{w}\n但凭着一番努力和力气，我终于重新站了起来。

column5: It doesn't overpower me like before. This time, I expect different.{w}\nLike Gryz said, it bends to the will of the wielder. Everything has changed.{w}\nI put the scabbard back on, but I hold onto the sword with a slight grin.
column6: 它不再像从前那样压制我了。这一次，我期待的是不同的结果。{w}\n正如格瑞兹所说，它屈从于持剑者的意志。一切都变了。{w}\n我重新背好剑鞘，却仍握着剑，嘴角微微上扬。

column5: I'm in control of it, now.
column6: 现在，我能掌控它了。

column5: No, I couldn't let him do this. My reasons were my own.{w}\nI shake my head, and hold the blade closer to my body.{w}\nHe sighs, and looks down at the floor, defeated.
column6: 不，我不能让他这么做。我有我自己的理由。{w}\n我摇摇头，把剑抱得更贴近身体。{w}\n他叹了口气，垂头看着地板，认输了。

column5: Very well...
column6: 好吧……

column5: He lets go of me, and I start to stumble.{w}\nI use the scabbard as a cane to hold myself up.{w}\nI can tell that he's angry, but also that he understands.
column6: 他松开我，我一时踉跄。{w}\n我把剑鞘当拐杖拄着，撑住身子。{w}\n我看得出他生气了，但也看得出他理解。

column5: I expected him to fight me for the blade, but he accepts defeat.{w}\nTurning around, he starts to walk away — his shoulders slumped down.{w}\nThis was my job. This was my destiny. To harness The Blade of Exodus.
column6: 我原以为他会为这把剑跟我争抢，可他却认输了。{w}\n他转过身，耷拉着肩膀，开始走开。{w}\n这是我的职责。这是我的命运。驾驭流亡之刃。

column5: I couldn't let others use it to assist in their suicide.{w}\nTurning to face the idol, I slowly remove the blade from the scabbard.{w}\nRemembering Gryz's insight, I try to bend the blade to my will.
column6: 我不能让别人用它来成全自己的送死。{w}\n我转身面对灵像，缓缓将剑从鞘中抽出。{w}\n忆起格瑞兹的见解，我试着让这把剑屈从于我的意志。

column5: This time, it wouldn't overpower me.{w}\nIt would help me save us all from this massacre.
column6: 这一次，它不会压制我。{w}\n它会帮我将所有人从这场屠杀中拯救出来。

column5: The flash of white light that I expected is nowhere to be found.{w}\nI can hold the blade with no trouble, just like I desired.{w}\nSo it was true — the blade is mine to control...?
column6: 我预想中的白光并未出现。{w}\n我能毫无阻碍地握住这把剑，正如我所愿。{w}\n看来这是真的——这把剑由我掌控……？

column5: With a wide smirk, I hold the blade up to the idol.{w}\nIt was time to destroy all of the Honor Guard in these tunnels.{w}\nIt was time to free the souls of all of the condemned. Our parents, too.
column6: 我咧嘴一笑，将剑举向灵像。{w}\n是时候摧毁这些隧道里所有的荣誉卫队了。{w}\n是时候解放所有被囚者的灵魂了。还有我们的父母。

column5: That desire in my mind sparks the blade, and the white light fills the room.{w}\nBut there's another desire, too. The survival of Damek, and our future victory.{w}\nThe ground shakes more violently, almost causing me to fall to the floor.
column6: 我心中的这份渴望点燃了剑，白光充满了整个房间。{w}\n但还有另一个渴望。达梅克的生还，以及我们未来的胜利。{w}\n地面震动得更加剧烈，几乎把我震倒在地。

column5: But I stand my ground. This was too important.{w}\nThe survival of The Rebellion, and Alestia's future, was on the line.{w}\nI'm too overcome with hope to falter, as the white light slowly subsides.
column6: 但我站稳脚跟。这太重要了。{w}\n反抗军的存亡，以及阿莱斯蒂亚的未来，都系于此。{w}\n白光缓缓消退，我心中满怀希望，绝不会动摇。

column5: The idol starts to flicker, like it's running out of power.{w}\nDid I do it...? I guess there's only one way to find out.{w}\nI put the scabbard back on, but I hold onto the sword.
column6: 灵像开始闪烁，仿佛能量即将耗尽。{w}\n我做到了吗……？我想只能亲自去确认了。{w}\n我重新背好剑鞘，却仍握着剑。

column5: I'm in control of it, now.
column6: 现在，我能掌控它了。

column5: I stand there, using the blade as a crutch.{w}\nWith the ground shaking so violently, it's hard to stand up.{w}\nI'll need to go back to the atrium. They need to know about this!
column6: 我站在那里，把剑当作拐杖。{w}\n地面震得如此厉害，很难站稳。{w}\n我得回中庭去。他们得知道这件事！

column5: No...! What have you done!?
column6: 不……！你干了什么！？

column5: Sovy charges into the room, catching me completely off guard.{w}\nHe stands there, panting, looking at the idol, and how it flickers.{w}\nWith a grunt of rage, he starts running at me, ready to attack.
column6: 索维冲进房间，完全出乎我的意料。{w}\n他站在那里喘着气，望着灵像，望着它如何闪烁。{w}\n他怒吼一声，朝我冲过来，准备动手。

column5: Because of the trembling earth, however, he stumbles a bit.{w}\nI use this to my advantage, and jump out of the way.{w}\nLanding with a quick roll, I'm back on my feet.
column6: 可由于地面震颤，他踉跄了一下。{w}\n我借此机会，闪身跳到一旁。{w}\n我快速翻滚落地，重新站稳。

column5: We circle around each other, both hesitant to attack.{w}\nI hold out the blade, as if to threaten him.
column6: 我们绕着彼此打转，都迟疑着不肯先动手。{w}\n我举起剑，像是在威胁他。

column5: There's so much you don't know.
column6: 你不知道的事太多了。

column5: He smirks, and lunges forward to attack me.{w}\nI hold out the blade to guard myself, but I'm not sure what happens next.{w}\nWith a snap of his fingers, mid-lunge, the blade suddenly vanishes from my hands.
column6: 他咧嘴一笑，扑上前来攻击我。{w}\n我举剑格挡，却不确定接下来会发生什么。{w}\n在他扑来的半途中，随着一声响指，那把剑突然从我手中消失了。

column5: A few moments later, it rematerializes in {i}his{/i}.{w}\nI don't have enough time to brace myself. It's already too late.{w}\nMoments later, I'm on the floor, with Sovy ontop of me.
column6: 片刻之后，它重新出现在{i}他{/i}手中。{w}\n我来不及稳住身形。已经太迟了。{w}\n片刻之后，我躺在地上，索维压在我身上。

column5: So he {i}can{/i} wield it. Just like the vision showed me.
column6: 原来他{i}确实{/i}能驾驭它。正如幻象所示。
